GenZ have unique characteristics in their behaviour from their older counterparts. In current era of AI and Internet smartphone has become an essential part of our life that connect us with the rest of the world as world has now become a global village. The smartphone industry is growing rapidly with new innovations and features every year or so. Pakistan as a developing country is filled with smartphones that are cheaper and has better features made possible by Chinese manufacturers. Young adults and Adults can now afford better smartphones at competitive prices. Data in this study was collected by the help of cross-sectional survey that include 70 smartphone users as subjects. Using Literature review we found that even though the purchase of a mobile phone is subjective there are some factors that influence the customers i.e. young adults, to switch brands. 
Study Indicated that Infinix has most loyal customer base as compared to other smartphone users and Apple is the most popular brand, The studies shows that the things that influence consumer switching behaviour of smart phones includes product quality as the primary factor. The study further reveals that customer satisfaction has positive affect on customer switching brands. Moreover, switching cost also played an important role.

articles.title: At The Mercy of Politics? When Policy Change  Undermines the Credibility of Public Managers
articles.authors: Mads Pieter van Luttervelt; Mathias Østergaard-Nielsen; Anders Grøn
articles.abstract: Politicians often change policies—sometimes unexpectedly—but how it affects the bureaucracy remains largely unknown. We argue that changing policies can undermine the credibility of public managers in the eyes of the street-level bureaucrats. Testing this argument causally in the real world is challenging as it requires unanticipated policy change that only affects part of the bureaucracy and a pre- and post-change measurement of relevant constructs. To overcome these challenges, we leverage a quasi-experimental design by exploiting that a nationwide reform in Denmark’s education sector was unexpectedly changed for half of the country’s high schools. We find a long-term negative causal effect of policy change on the credibility of public managers, when they showed commitment to the initial policy. The effect is driven by street-level bureaucrats whose policy preferences align with the initial policy. We discuss trade-offs for policy makers and managers when initiating or responding to policy changes.

articles.title: Book Review: A Marxist Critique of the Ruined University, by Krystian Szadkowski and Jakub Krzeski, Springer, 2025.
articles.authors: Anıl Kandemir
articles.abstract: This abstract summarizes a review of Krystian Szadkowski and Jakub Krzeski’s A Marxist Critique of the Ruined University (2025), a pivotal theoretical intervention that reconceptualizes the modern decline of higher education. Rather than lamenting the loss of historical academic ideals, the reviewed text posits that the university is experiencing a profound ontological crisis driven fundamentally by the imperatives of global capital accumulation. The review highlights how the authors map the academy's systemic reorganization into a primary node for value reproduction, where knowledge and academic labor are continuously co-opted to serve market interests. To navigate this crisis, Szadkowski and Krzeski deploy a Marxian "integral critique" composed of three dialectical stages: in (diagnosing internal institutional mechanisms and exploitation), against (resisting internal hierarchies), and beyond (identifying emerging social relations). The review traces the book’s eleven chapters through conceptual, foundational, tactical, and reconstructive clusters. It emphasizes the authors' uncompromising dissection of the "Academic Robinson"—a mode of subjectivation marked by hyper-individualization—and the alienating forces of neoliberal metricization that fundamentally transform institutional habitus. Crucially, the review notes that the book avoids deterministic pessimism by offering an affirmative, emancipatory blueprint. By moving beyond mere melancholic observation, the authors envision a post-capitalist "university of the common" anchored in horizontal governance, alternative property relations, and collective social production. Ultimately, the review concludes that this robust analytical toolkit successfully bridges abstract philosophical diagnosis with the urgent material need for transformative praxis and collective solidarity among academic laborers.

articles.title: Bioplastics as a Sustainability Promise: Promises and (Dis)illusionments of a ‘Technological Fix’ in Germany
articles.authors: Yannick Kalff
articles.abstract: Bioplastics have emerged as a beacon of hope for sustainable alternatives to conventional,petroleum-based  plastics. They promise sustainability by technically addressing the issues associated with plastics – waste burden, emissions, and dependence on oil. This makes them a ‘technological fix,’ recommending simple technical solutions to complex challenges but overlooking the intricate reality. The article empirically demonstrates that the disappointments with bioplastics are not solely due to technical reasons but stem from neglected societal, social, economic, or ecological factors. These factors range from the material properties of early bioplastics, monocultures and land competition for the use of renewable resources, to their economic competitiveness. From the technological promise of sustainability and the dashed hopes for bioplastics, it follows that the technological fix fails because it is tied to the path dependencies of fossil plastics. Without social innovations in societal use of plastics, departing from these paths is difficult.

articles.title: The Impact of Inflation on Income Distribution in Nigeria. An Empirical Approach (1990–2023)
articles.authors: Adriel Ekozin; Felix I. Ifada; James A. Adesokan
articles.abstract: The study examined the impact of inflation on income in Nigeria for the period of 1990–2023. The study made use of four explanatory variables, which are: external remittance, interest rate, inflation rate, and exchange rate on income in Nigeria. The data were obtained from various issues of the Central Bank of Nigeria (CBN) Statistical Bulletin, journals, as well as financial indicators. Augmented Dickey-Fuller (ADF) and Johansen cointegration tests were employed to confirm the stationarity of the series and the long-run relationship among the series. The findings indicate that remittances positively impact economic growth and income distribution, supporting household consumption and investment. Higher interest rates increase the cost of borrowing, limiting access to credit, reducing investment, and negatively impacting income distribution. High inflation reduces household purchasing power, particularly affecting low-income earners, thereby worsening income distribution. The study therefore concluded that remittances play a crucial role in boosting real GDP and improving household welfare, emphasising the need for policies that facilitate their inflow. Conversely, high interest rates, inflation, and exchange-rate volatility negatively impact economic growth and exacerbate income inequality. The study therefore recommended that the Central Bank of Nigeria should implement policies to reduce transaction costs and encourage diaspora investments. The apex bank should also promote financial-sector reforms to lower borrowing costs and boost investment. The government should enhance domestic production to stabilise prices and reduce inflationary pressures.

articles.title: Changing governments, stable elites? Executive personnel continuity in global perspective
articles.authors: Marco Improta
articles.abstract: In political science, government change is typically understood as a shift in who holds power, even though new cabinets may formally include many members of the previous governing elite. In this study, I differentiate institutional turnover from personnel turnover by reconstructing transitions between successive governments using the WhoGov dataset. I introduce an Executive Personnel Continuity Index (EPCI) that measures the similarity between outgoing and incoming ministerial rosters. I argue that leader succession functions as an executive reset: new leaders have incentives to establish control, reward loyalists, and signal political change. Party organizations, however, can insulate incumbent ministers from replacement. I test these expectations using descriptive evidence, country and transition-year fixed effects, equal-country weighting, entropy balancing and a transition-centered comparison with the outgoing government's own pre-transition continuity. Across the principal specifications, leader replacement is associated with a decline of approximately one-third in executive personnel continuity. The decline is limited under same-party succession, substantially larger across party boundaries and greatest under complete partisan alternation. The findings therefore indicate that a change in government translates into a substantive transformation of the elite mainly when it also unsettles the leadership and party bases of executive power, and this has significant consequences for political systems worldwide.

articles.title: Shaping the notion of #wellbeing in the therapy culture context: an analysis through Instagram narratives
articles.authors: Ainara Larrondo-Ureta; Simón Peña-Fernández; Jordi Morales-i-Gras
articles.abstract:
Purpose – The aim of this paper is to (1) identify textual and visual themes and sub-themes associated with the #wellbeing hashtag on Instagram, (2) assess their varying levels of engagement and (3) investigate gender bias present in the analysed visual narratives.
Design/methodology/approach – This study employs a range of big data analysis techniques to investigate various dimensions of wellbeing on Instagram. Initially, a sample of 9,844 posts was processed using data mining and text analysis methods to identify and categorise significant hashtags, which facilitated the classification of posts into thematic clusters through hierarchical clustering. Engagement was then assessed using non-parametric statistical tests. Additionally, computer vision models were used to analyse and classify visual narratives, grouping images into communities based on visual similarities. Finally, gender representation in the images was examined using object detection models.
Findings – The study reveals that the discourse around #wellbeing on Instagram is predominantly feminised and focuses primarily on mental, psychological and spiritual aspects. Therapeutic and positive psychology narratives are the most prevalent and engaging, while physical activity and nutrition play a relatively secondary role. Two major macro-narratives emerge: firstly, mental health and emotional wellbeing, often featuring hashtags related to therapy, self-discovery, spirituality and motivational quotes; secondly, though less prominently, themes and visual narratives concerning physical activity and healthy habits, emphasising exercise and nutrition.
Originality/value – The study identifies, for the first time in the academic literature, key themes and subthemes in the textual and visual narratives on wellness on the social media (Instagram), offering evidence for its feminisation. These findings contribute to the academic discussion on the implications of the notion of wellbeing on Instagram in relation to “therapy culture”. This idea can be applied to other social media, as well as to other areas, such as working life, where diverse individualities and groups also coexist.

articles.title: “ChatGPT has helped me more than 15 years of therapy”:   AI therapy and moving beyond para-social interaction to conceptualising AI chatbots as a significant other.
articles.authors: Stephanie Alice Baker; Michael James Walsh
articles.abstract: There is a growing body of literature that assesses the risks and ethical challenges associated with AI therapy and the integration of artificial intelligence (AI) into healthcare. Much of this research examines the risks and harms associated with parasocial relationships and projecting sentient qualities onto AI chatbots. This article makes a novel contribution to this literature by examining AI therapy from an ethnographic perspective, examining how people strategically use prompts to reduce the perceived risks associated with AI therapy. Analysing TikTok videos (n = 840) to understand how content creators use AI to support their mental health, our study found that most people use AI therapy for personality analysis and self-improvement rather than medical treatment and diagnosis. Although users demonstrated reflexivity and agency in their therapeutic engagement with AI, we introduce the concept of AI as a ‘significant other’ to highlight the impact of AI therapy.

articles.title: Taxation of the Digital Economy in Nigeria: A Conceptual Review
articles.authors: Adriel Ekozin; Simeon Funminiyi Akinpelu; Igbinosun Friday Ese
articles.abstract: This study examined the taxation of the digital economy in Nigeria through a conceptual review, focusing on challenges, prospects, and policy implications of taxing digital activities including e-commerce, fintech, streaming services, online advertising, and social media commerce. The purpose was to critically analyse how Nigeria’s legal and regulatory frameworks, administrative capacities, and technological tools interact to facilitate revenue mobilisation from digital economic activities. A qualitative conceptual research design was employed, relying entirely on secondary data from academic journals, government reports, Finance Acts, and international frameworks, with data analysed through content and thematic analysis and supported by descriptive statistics from government and global sources. Findings revealed that while Nigeria’s digital economy has expanded rapidly, compliance with tax obligations remains moderate, with informal platforms and cross border transactions limiting effective revenue collection. Legal recognition of significant economic presence is crucial for capturing digital taxes, yet enforcement gaps and limited technological monitoring hinder compliance, with fintech platforms integrated into formal banking systems showing higher adherence than informal social media commerce. The study contributes a structured conceptual framework linking digital activities, regulatory clarity, administrative enforcement, and revenue outcomes, while identifying critical policy and practical gaps. The findings imply that improving technological monitoring, strengthening legal frameworks, and enhancing stakeholder engagement are essential for increasing compliance, offering insights for policymakers and laying the foundation for future research on sustainable digital taxation strategies in Nigeria.

articles.title: Machine-translated ParlSpeech V2 dataset: Full-text corpora of 3.5 million parliamentary speeches from seven countries translated into English
articles.authors: Štěpán Štěpán Jabůrek; Adam Černý; Christian Rauh; Jan Schwalbach
articles.abstract: Machine-translated ParlSpeech V2 contains complete full-text vectors of more than 3.5 million parliamentary speeches in the key legislative chambers of Austria, the Czech Republic, Germany, Denmark, the Netherlands, Spain, and Sweden, covering periods between 21 and 32 years. The data include speeches machine-translated into English using open-source OPUS-MT models. Original language speeches from ParlSpeech V2 (Rauh & Schwalbach 2020) are present alongside the English translation. Meta-data include the original information on date, speaker, party, and partially agenda item under which a speech was held. The accompanying release note provides a more detailed guide to the data.

articles.title: Enabling justice in nature-positive transformations: Insights from agricultural, forestry, and health transitions
articles.authors: Aniek Hebinck; Thomas Fransen; Dalia D'Amato; Ben Delbaere; Symke Nieboer; Lara Lebleu; Stella Piipponen-Doyle; Valentina Vaglica; Hans Keune; Opi Outhwaite
articles.abstract: Transformations within the biodiversity nexus are increasingly expected to deliver not only environmental outcomes but also enable justice. Yet, how justice is experienced and shaped within such transformation processes remains unclear. This paper examines how justice is experienced and shaped in practice across three nature-positive transitions in Europe: efforts to make agriculture, forestry, and healthcare more supportive of biodiversity and human wellbeing. Drawing on a relational approach to justice and insights from just transitions, the analysis shows that policy rarely explicitly aims to enable justice. Instead, policies often indirectly aim to promote justice through low-conflict and incremental pathways. Across the cases, procedural dimensions dominate in policy approaches to enable justice, while distributive and recognition dimensions are addressed unevenly and less consistently in the policy frameworks analysed. At the same time, justice appears to be shaped and experienced less by individual policy instruments than by broader structural conditions, including institutional arrangements, property relations, and dominant knowledge frameworks, which influence how policies are implemented and whose interests they serve. Building on these findings, the paper conceptualises justice as a relational and context-dependent phenomenon, produced through interactions between actor framings, institutional arrangements, and transition dynamics. This highlights key tensions between ambition for just transformation and governance approaches that prioritise incremental and low conflict pathways, with important implications for both research and policy.

articles.title: Harm Through the “#RizzCam”: Smart Glasses, Ambient Capture and Invisible Harassment
articles.authors: Milica Stilinovic; Ben Egliston; Wenqi Tan; Marcus Carter; Joanne E. Gray
articles.abstract: In online safety research, harassment is commonly understood as involving overt and unwanted acts that create a hostile environment for individuals or groups. Smart glasses, or wearable digital devices that are often indistinguishable from ordinary eyewear but can record video, audio and location data in real time, enable new forms of online harassment and gender-based harms that may not be recognised by current online safety or platform governance frameworks. Drawing on an interpretive content analysis of 350 point-of-view Instagram videos posted by individuals self-associated with the pick-up artistry (PUA) community, we examine how smart glasses can be used to harass women through what we call ambient capture. Ambient capture includes clandestine recording of people and social interactions within public, semi-private and private spaces. We argue this can constitute harassment when it is targeted at women and shared online without their consent. In our study, we found videos using ambient capture practices to harass women that had gone undetected by Instagram’s content moderation systems. These findings suggest online safety regimes and content moderation approaches should be assessed to ensure they account for the more invisible forms of harassment introduced by smart glasses and other wearable technologies.

articles.title: From science-policy to science-policy-society: enabling transformative change in practice
articles.authors: Aniek Hebinck; Mara de Pater; Anita Lazurko; Gijs Diercks; Dalia D'Amato; Amanda Krijgsman; Heli Saarikoski; Hans Keune; Symke Nieboer; Julia Wittmayer
articles.abstract: Transformative change is widely recognised as necessary to address interconnected, persistent sustainability crises. Yet, despite growing experimentation with co-production and societal engagement, dominant science–policy arrangements remain largely assessment-oriented and geared toward incremental optimisation. While the 2024 IPBES Transformative Change Assessment was a landmark articulating drivers and principles of transformation, less attention has been paid to how science–policy interfaces themselves must reorganise to enable transformative action. This perspective addresses that gap. We argue that enabling transformative change requires reconfiguring the science–policy interface toward a science–policy–society interface embedding collaboration, experimentation, and collective learning. Drawing on insights from transformative research and our own transdisciplinary experiences, we propose three institutional conditions: (1) embracing the contested nature of transformative change as a productive space; (2) shifting research and policy from incremental improvements to transformative futures and emerging alternatives; and (3) institutionalizing reciprocal, action-oriented collaboration that enables sustained experimentation and collective agency. These conditions must be reinforced through institutional reforms in agenda-setting, funding and evaluation logics, and mechanisms ensuring continuity and societal memory. We conclude that institutional reform and transformative practice co-evolve, positioning science–policy–society configurations as enabling infrastructures for sustainability transformations.

articles.title: Accounting for Compositional Bias in Unexpected Event During Survey Designs
articles.authors: Klara Müller
articles.abstract: Political events may affect not only people’s political attitudes and behavior but also who responds to surveys. If events change who participates, estimates from event-focused designs may reflect changes in sample compositions rather than genuine opinion change. This is particularly challenging for designs like the Unexpected Event during Survey Design (UESD), which identifies causal effects by comparing respondents interviewed immediately before and after an unexpected event. I develop an analytical framework that extends established UESD best-practices, which successfully address observable differences between these samples, by sensitivity analyses to assess the potential impact of unobserved compositional bias. I illustrate the framework using the 2015 Charlie Hebdo terrorist attacks to estimate rally-around-the-flag effects and demonstrate its broader applicability by replicating 14 published UESD studies on terrorist events and rally-type outcomes. Across cases, political events affect sample compositions, but accounting for observable differences rarely changes estimated effects. Further, unobserved compositional bias would typically need to be implausibly strong to overturn substantive results. The proposed framework provides tools to assess and mitigate compositional bias, which strengthens causal inference in UESD and other event-focused designs.

articles.title: A Bayesian Model to Estimate Male and Female Fertility Patterns at a Subnational Level
articles.authors: Riccardo Omenti; Monica Alexander; Nicola Barban
articles.abstract: Accurate subnational fertility estimates are crucial for shaping policy decisions across diverse sectors, including education, health care, and social welfare. However, these estimates are difficult to obtain in small populations, in which data on births classified by maternal and paternal ages may be lacking or inadequate. In this paper, we describe a Bayesian model tailored to estimate the Total Fertility Rates (TFR) for both men and women at a subnational level. The model relies on population counts from age-sex pyramids and jointly models mortality and fertility patterns while accounting for uncertainty and spatiotemporal dependencies. Testing the model with simulated data that mimic Australian regions, as well as with real data from US counties, Mexican states and Nigerian regions, demonstrates its ability to generate reasonable TFR estimates. The estimates produced have straightforward applications to the study of subregional reproductive disparities, and the proposed modeling framework can be extended to investigate subnational fertility patterns across other countries with limited or fragmented birth data.

articles.title: Constrained Agency under Existential Threat: Immigrant Entrepreneurship and Expulsion
articles.authors: Robertson Khan Tengeh
articles.abstract: Structural and socio-cultural constraints have long shaped African immigrant entrepreneurship in South Africa. The organised anti-foreigner campaigns of 2025–2026 echoed the earlier expulsions in Ghana (1969) and Nigeria (1983). What made them different was that the host society itself became the organised source of existential threat. This article aimed to develop a theoretical framework accounting for how entrepreneurial agency changes when organised political mobilisation simultaneously threatens physical safety, legal presence, and venture survival. The framework was developed as a conceptual model by drawing on constrained agency theory alongside scholarship on institutions, social movements, scapegoating, and moral panic. Rather than being tested with primary data, it was illustrated through historical and contemporary African cases. CAT-ET suggests that when constraints become existential, agency tends to shift towards either adaptive persistence or strategic exit. Two interacting mechanisms were specified: functional institutional inaccessibility under violence, whereby protective institutions remained operational but selectively inaccessible, and the entrepreneur-as-symbol dynamic, whereby immigrant ventures became politically constructed as emblems of economic grievance. CAT-ET reframed organised expulsion as a recurring political-economic process and offered a basis for comparative research across the Global South.

articles.title: Understanding moral trade-offs in pandemic response: A discrete choice experiment on avian influenza policies
articles.authors: Nicholas Smeele; Charlotte Nina Maria Waltz; Anja Schreijer; Pearl A. Dykstra
articles.abstract: Pandemic preparedness requires navigating trade-offs between health, economic, and social impacts; choices that often involve moral tensions. This study investigates how the Dutch public evaluates such trade-offs in the context of a potential outbreak of highly pathogenic avian influenza (HPAI). Using a discrete choice experiment (DCE) administered to a representative sample of 1,045 respondents from the LISS panel, we examined preferences across six policy outcomes: mortality, lasting physical and mental injuries, postponed healthcare, social restrictions, and one-off tax payments. A latent class logit model identified four distinct preference profiles, revealing substantial heterogeneity in moral and economic reasoning. Two classes exhibited taboo trade-off aversion (TTOA) when values such as life or human dignity were traded against monetary costs. Respondents displaying TTOA emphasized solidarity and governmental responsibility, while cost-sensitive groups prioritized economic efficiency. These findings highlight that public acceptance of pandemic policies depends not only on effectiveness and cost but also on perceived moral legitimacy. Accounting for TTOA in economic evaluation can improve the ethical considerations and societal acceptability of future pandemic preparedness strategies.

articles.title: Revisiting the Social Security Claiming Puzzle: Behavioral Preferences as Rational Explanations for Early Claiming
articles.authors: Derek Tharp
articles.abstract: Nearly one-fourth of Americans claim Social Security at age 62, while only one-in-ten wait until age 70—a pattern that has long puzzled economists who argue delay is financially optimal. This paper develops a series of dynamic programming models to examine whether early claiming reflects mistakes or rational responses to preferences overlooked in standard analyses. Three behavioral factors are incorporated: a claim-retire linkage (a preference to claim benefits at retirement rather than managing a separate "bridge" period); front-loaded consumption preferences (a desire to spend more in the early, active years of retirement); and source-dependent utility (greater comfort spending from regular income like Social Security than drawing down a retirement portfolio). Using Epstein–Zin recursive utility with stochastic investment returns, medical expenditure shocks, mortality risk, policy risk, and bequest motives, results show that incorporating these empirically documented factors substantially lowers optimal claiming ages. Under the full behavioral specification, claiming at 62 is optimal for households with up to $800,000 in initial wealth—a wealth level that encompasses the vast majority of Americans approaching retirement. Results are qualitatively robust to alternative assumptions about mortality, bequest strength, tax treatment, and spousal or survivor benefits. These findings suggest that widespread early claiming may reflect genuine preferences rather than financial mistakes, though individual circumstances—including wealth, employment status, tax situation, and personal preferences—may provide incentives toward delay. Rather than uniformly prescribing delay, advisors should assess clients' goals, circumstances, and preferences and tailor recommendations accordingly.

articles.title: Beyond Encampment? Understanding Attitudes Toward Refugee Integration
articles.authors: Mae MacDonald; Adam G Lichtenheld
articles.abstract: Most of the world's refugees live in low- and middle-income countries, where debates center on integrating those already present rather than admitting new arrivals. Yet existing research focuses largely on admission in high-income countries. We provide one of the first nationwide assessments of attitudes toward integration in the Global South, drawing on a survey of 3,326 Kenyans fielded after a reform was passed but before implementation, with embedded experiments varying policy dimension and refugee group. Support for integration is high, but citizens are less supportive of allowing refugees to leave camps than granting economic inclusion or creating integrated settlements, and support varies significantly by refugee nationality. Opposition is driven primarily by fears of crime, terrorism, and the spread of conflict. Ethnic kinship and close contact predict support, while economic factors matter little. These findings suggest that integration is politically feasible, but insecurity associated with free movement remains the largest concern.

articles.title: Macroeconomic Volatility and Organizational Performance: A Contingency Theory Perspective from the Nigerian Corporate Sector
articles.authors: Adriel Ekozin; Philip Shakede Sanni; Friday Izen Ohiokha
articles.abstract: Macroeconomic instability has continued to shape the operating environment of firms in Nigeria, creating uncertainty that affects business outcomes. This study examines the effect of macroeconomic volatility on organizational performance in the Nigerian corporate sector, while also considering the role of firm-level characteristics within a contingency theory framework. A longitudinal panel design was adopted, using secondary data obtained from the Central Bank of Nigeria, the World Bank, and financial reports of selected firms listed on the Nigerian Exchange over the period 2010–2024. Panel regression techniques were employed, including fixed and random effects models, with the Hausman test used to determine the appropriate specification. The findings indicate that macroeconomic volatility, particularly inflation, exchange rate fluctuations, and interest rate changes, has a significant negative effect on firm performance, while economic growth exerts a positive influence. The results further show that firm-level factors such as size, liquidity, and leverage significantly moderate this relationship. Firms with stronger financial capacity are better able to absorb macroeconomic shocks, whereas highly leveraged firms are more vulnerable to instability. The study concludes that organizational performance in Nigeria is influenced not only by external economic conditions but also by how firms adjust their internal structures and strategies. By applying contingency theory, the study provides a more nuanced explanation of performance differences across firms. The findings offer useful insights for managers seeking to improve resilience and for policymakers aiming to strengthen the business environment.

articles.title: El dolor que no se hereda: la intransmisibilidad de la acción indemnizatoria del daño moral (comentario a la sentencia de la Corte Suprema de 27 de julio de 2026, rol N° 32.205-2025)
articles.authors: Andrés Gabriel Varas Quijón
articles.abstract: La Primera Sala de la Corte Suprema, en sentencia de 27 de julio de 2026 (rol N° 32.205-2025, redacción del abogado integrante Álvaro Vidal Olivares), acogió un recurso de casación en el fondo y declaró que la acción indemnizatoria del daño moral que la víctima no ejerció en vida es intransmisible a sus herederos. El caso —una paciente a la que, por omisión de la pausa de seguridad, se le extirpó el riñón sano y se le dejó el tumoral, falleciendo semanas después— había sido resuelto en ambas instancias por la tesis contraria. La Corte funda la intransmisibilidad en dos pilares: la naturaleza personalísima del interés lesionado, que hace intransferible el fundamento mismo de la acción, y la finalidad compensatoria de la indemnización, que sólo puede cumplirse en la persona que padeció el daño; la sede normativa es sucesoria, y descansa en el adjetivo «transmisibles» de los artículos 951 inciso segundo y 1097 inciso primero del Código Civil, reforzado por el criterio biográfico de avaluación del artículo 41 de la Ley N° 19.966. De allí extrae dos corolarios: ni el contenido pecuniario de la prestación ni el ingreso de la acción al patrimonio del causante determinan su transmisibilidad. La tutela de los cercanos queda reconducida íntegramente al daño por repercusión o rebote —derecho propio y originario, que exige probar vínculo afectivo estrecho y no puede acumularse con la pretensión hereditaria—, mientras el daño emergente reclamado iure hereditatis quedó firme. Este trabajo reconstruye el caso y su iter, sistematiza la ratio decidendi y sus consecuencias, sitúa la decisión en el vaivén jurisprudencial chileno de las dos últimas décadas y en el espejo comparado —donde Francia e Italia habrían transmitido con estos mismos hechos—, y cierra con un decálogo de litigación. La tesis, para quien demanda: el Código hace de los herederos los continuadores de la persona del causante, pero se sucede el patrimonio, no la biografía.

articles.title: The Rise and (Partial) Retreat of DEI Claims in Recruiting
articles.authors: Janet Xu; Reuben Hurst; Shanshan Liu
articles.abstract: In recent years, and especially after the 2020 Black Lives Matter protests, U.S. employers increasingly affirmed commitments to diversity, equity, and inclusion (DEI). Donald Trump's second administration has sought to reverse this shift. Yet how far pro-diversity language actually rose in employers' recruiting, and how much of that rise has since been undone, has not been established. Drawing on the universe of U.S. online job postings between January 2016 and February 2026-371.1 million postings from 2.7 million employers-we find that pro-diversity claims appeared in 7-12% of job postings until mid-2020, then rose 152% to a peak of 25.4% postings on the eve of the 2024 election. They fell 21% thereafter, to 19.9% by February 2026. Declines were sharper among federal contractors but proportionally similar for Democratic-and Republican-leaning employers. The reversal is unprecedented, yet partial: it has undone roughly a third of the post-2020 rise, but pro-diversity claims remain twice as common as they were pre-2020.

articles.title: “Ascending dragon or blasting the dragon vein?”: How Chinese netizens construct environmental meanings in digital publics
articles.authors: Yingnian Tao; Mark Ryan
articles.abstract: Corporations’ sustainability communication is increasingly challenged by digital publics. Yet research on how netizens contest corporate sustainability narratives, and thereby construct environmental meanings, remains largely confined to Western contexts. This study addresses this gap by examining Chinese netizens’ discursive responses to a controversial fireworks display in the Himalayas staged by international mountaineering brand Arc’teryx. Comments from the seven most popular Weibo posts were selected to compile a corpus (140,584 tokens),  and analysed through corpus-assisted discourse analysis, particularly keyword and concordance analysis. Findings show that netizens mobilise multiple meaning systems to express strong disapproval, including scientific ecological knowledge, perceptions of environmental governance failure, spiritual-cultural references, consumer action, and nationalism. These interconnected meaning systems converge around a distinctive feature of Chinese digital environmentalism: a nature-centred view of human-nature relations and harmony. The study extends understanding of digital environmentalism beyond Western contexts by showing that environmental meanings in Chinese digital spaces are place- and culture-based, intertwining ecological concerns with emotion, spiritual wellbeing, perceptions of justice, and national interests.

articles.title: Gender Bias and Stereotyping in Portrayals of Female Physicists: An International Analysis from 2019-2022
articles.authors: Rishika Porandla
articles.abstract: This research quantifies the presence of pervasive gender biases and discriminatory depictions within the field of physics through the analysis of media representations. Utilizing a dataset spanning 2019-2022 in Mali, India, Peru, and Singapore, the study employs natural language processing techniques to identify instances of biased language, particularly indicative of assumptions of biological determinism (BD) and childhood socialization (CS). Findings reveal more pronounced BD/CS-insinuating diction in lower HDI regions, ranging from 21% in Mali to 0.8% in Singapore. Female physicist representation in academic literature averaged 11.9%, with first authorship rates varying from 0.2% in Mali to 23.2% in Singapore. Negative depictions persisted despite a 27% increase in references to female physicists, highlighting the need for targeted interventions to counteract prejudice and foster inclusive environments within the physics community in order to promote gender equity and harness diverse perspectives in advancing research, development, and scientific innovation.

articles.title: Social network involvement in abortion care-seeking and abortion outcomes among a population-based sample in Nigeria
articles.authors: Selena Anjur-Dietrich; Funmilola Olaolorun; Elizabeth Omoluabi; Philip Anglewicz; Suzanne Bell
articles.abstract: People often engage social networks when navigating structural and local abortion access constraints, but limited research links this involvement to abortion outcomes. This cross-sectional study analyzed PMA2020 data from 1,144 women in Nigeria who had abortions, identified via population-based surveys and abortion-focused follow-ups conducted in 2018. We examined how social network involvement in care-seeking—specifically, participation in selecting method or provider—related to abortion outcomes: medically defined abortion safety, use of preferred method and provider, and success of the initial abortion attempt. Social network involvement was common (63%) and varied across sociodemographic characteristics. Outcomes differed by who participated: when both partners and family/friends participated, women were least likely to have the least safe abortions (23.9% vs. 60.9%, p<0.001) or require multiple attempts (13.7% vs. 19.1%, p=0.009), though equally likely to use preferred care compared to those seeking care alone. Partner-only involvement was also associated with fewer least safe abortions (36.3% vs. 60.9%, p<0.001), while family/friend-only involvement was linked to lower preference fulfillment (36.6% vs. 21.6%, p<0.001) and more repeated attempts (27.8% vs. 19.1%, p=0.038). These findings suggest that social networks have the potential to improve or worsen abortion outcomes, with important variation across person-centered measures of abortion experiences.

articles.title: Irregular Migration Early Warning Systems Based on Digital Migration Intelligence: Evidence from the 2026 Ceuta Crisis
articles.authors: Tado Jurić
articles.abstract:
Irregular migration crises often evolve more rapidly than conventional migration monitoring systems can detect. Although official migration statistics remain indispensable for documenting realised migration flows, they are typically published only after migration events have unfolded, limiting their value for anticipatory migration governance. This study proposes Digital Migration Intelligence as an integrated conceptual and analytical framework for the development of Irregular Migration Early Warning Systems and examines its applicability through the 2026 Ceuta migration crisis.
The study combines multilingual Google Trends analyses with evidence derived from Facebook communities and Meta Audience Insights. Rather than relying on isolated search terms, the proposed framework analyses the convergence of multilingual behavioural, communication and demographic digital traces, including destination-related, border-related, environmental, route-related and legal-information searches originating from Morocco, Algeria and Mauritania.
The findings suggest that migration-related digital activity intensified several days before the documented escalation of migration pressure. The strongest convergence of multilingual digital indicators was observed in Morocco, while comparable patterns in Algeria and a more limited signal in Mauritania provided additional support for the proposed analytical framework. Facebook communities revealed active communication networks through which migration-related information circulated, whereas Meta Audience Insights contributed complementary demographic evidence on language-specific digital populations.
The principal contribution of the study is the development of Digital Migration Intelligence as a multidimensional framework integrating behavioural, communication and demographic digital evidence within a single analytical perspective. The Ceuta case provides a proof of concept illustrating how multilingual digital traces may complement existing migration monitoring by identifying behavioural changes preceding rapidly evolving irregular migration crises. Future research should prospectively evaluate the framework across different migration corridors and assess its integration with artificial intelligence-assisted monitoring systems.
Keywords: Irregular Migration, Migration Early Warning Systems; Digital Migration Intelligence; irregular migration; digital demography; Big Data; Ceuta.

articles.title: Salient Shock, Imperceptible Impacts: Germans' Immigration Attitudes and the 2022-2023 Energy Price Spike
articles.authors: Niloufar Davis; William Matthew Halm; Hanno Hilbig; Daniel Hopkins
articles.abstract: Prior research finds that personal economic experiences typically have limited political impacts but can shape attitudes under certain conditions. Here, we explore a likely case: in Germany, Russia's 2022 invasion of Ukraine led to a dramatic spike in energy prices and an influx of Ukrainian refugees, both widely covered by news media. We use an online panel of German citizens (2022-2024) to assess the energy shock's impacts on immigration attitudes. Living in areas with larger natural gas price increases (and so higher residential heating costs) is associated with heightened economic distress. Yet we find no systematic evidence that these shocks shifted immigration attitudes over the subsequent 20 months, with minimum detectable effects of 0.10 to 0.18 standard deviations across our five attitude indices. Although extant research documents sizable political responses to some economic shocks, even a large, salient economic shock need not generate exclusionary immigration attitudes.

articles.title: Racializing Surveillance: Flock Camera Deployment, Black Population Geography, and the Limits of the Homicide Rationale in Hampton Roads
articles.authors: Andrew F. Baird; Steven Keener; John Finn
articles.abstract: This study examines the racialized geography of automatic license plate reader (ALPR) surveillance in Hampton Roads, Virginia. We link court-unsealed Flock Safety camera locations to measures from the 2020–2024 American Community Survey and the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention’s 2022–2024 National Vital Statistics System. Population-adjusted negative binomial models with locality-clustered standard errors and Webb wild-cluster bootstrap p-values test associations with racial composition, poverty, age structure, homicide and overdose mortality, and Black/White neighborhood boundaries. Camera counts are consistently higher in areas with larger Black populations and those bordering substantially Blacker communities, net of all covariates. Homicide mortality is not positively associated with cameras in the fully controlled model, whereas overdose mortality is. These findings challenge race-neutral claims that ALPR cameras merely follow serious violence and support theories of racializing surveillance by showing how data-driven public-safety infrastructure can reproduce racial inequalities in surveillance exposure.

articles.title: Against Mechanical Subjectivity: The Misalignment of Generative AI as a Tool for Qualitative Research
articles.authors: Bryce Clayton Newell; Torin Monahan; Lanore Hahn
articles.abstract: Interpretive and constructivist research is under assault from forces within and outside the qualitative research enterprise. Scholars, including those identifying as interpretive or constructivist scholars, have aligned themselves with positivist and metric-oriented scientists in promoting the use of generative artificial intelligence (GenAI or LLM) technologies in ways that sacrifice human-based knowledge production. We characterize this as the pursuit of mechanical subjectivity: the spurious premise of delegating subjective interpretive analysis and experience to AI machines. In this paper, we outline the ongoing debate in existing research; examine the frictions that GenAI creates with science as a social practice; discuss the implied epistemologies of GenAI tools and their misalignment with interpretive and constructivist research; and address how neoliberal logics shape AI adoption in university contexts. From a Critical Data Studies orientation, we argue that using LLMs for conducting qualitative data coding and analysis, writing up such analyses, or synthesizing ideas and conclusions is incompatible with the epistemological and ontological commitments necessary for conducting interpretive and constructivist research. We contend that mobilizing GenAI tools in ways that fully or partially replace humans in the knowledge production process—or that mediate the generative aspects of knowledge production between human researchers and their data—while claiming an interpretive or constructivist positionality amounts to scholarly malpractice, producing epistemic injustice.

articles.title: Cross-cultural survey research: The impact of translator background and competencies on questionnaire translation and post-editing quality
articles.authors: Ulrike Efu Nkong; Dorothée Behr; Anke Radinger
articles.abstract: Questionnaires in different languages are at the heart of cross-cultural survey research. To ensure their comparability and comprehensibility, translation procedures have continuously been optimized. However, the impact of a translator’s competencies on questionnaire translation and post-editing quality has, to date, not been systematically examined. With the aim to optimize team compositions, this study looks at the very first step of the TRAPD process – initial translations and the translators producing them. In an in-between translation experiment, 16 professional translators and 16 social scientists (with different levels of questionnaire experience) translated an experimental questionnaire containing 45 items partly from scratch and partly neural machine translation output was post-edited (i.e., corrected). To explore how a large language model (LLM) compares, additionally a raw LLM version was generated. After a blind expert assessment of the translations, error counts across different categories were compared and showed that overall error counts were comparable but professional translators, drawing on their translation expertise, produced significantly fewer linguistic errors (linguistic conventions, style and register) in translations produced from scratch. Experience with the questionnaire genre tended to help both professional groups to improve their results. Both professional groups performed similarly when post-editing machine translated text. The LLM-generated translation contained fewer errors overall than the median of human translations.

articles.title: Impact of Information Technology on Human Resource Management Practices in the Construction Industry in Edo State
articles.authors: Adriel Ekozin; Grace Motunrayo Opia; Monday Osemeke
articles.abstract: This study investigated the adoption and impact of information technology (IT) on Human Resource Management (HRM) practices in the construction industry in Edo State, Nigeria. A descriptive survey design was employed, targeting 500 HR professionals, with a stratified random sample of 222 respondents. Structured questionnaires validated for content and reliability (Cronbach’s α = 0.97) were used to collect data on demographics, IT usage in HR functions, and perceived IT impact. Out of 222 questionnaires, 196 were returned (88.3%). Findings revealed that IT is widely integrated into core HR functions, with payroll management (86.7%), employee records (81.6%), and attendance tracking (79.1%) most supported, and 81.6% of respondents using technology frequently. Regression analyses showed that IT adoption significantly predicts the frequency of HR technology use (R² = 0.425) and improves HRM effectiveness and efficiency (R² = 0.659). Payroll management, performance appraisal, and employee records were the strongest contributors. Despite high adoption, resistance to new technologies persists, indicating a need for training and change management.

articles.title: Global trends of Publications on Online Dating Violence – A Bibliometric Analysis
articles.authors: Yatheesh bharadwaj; Sivaranjini M; Jeevanthi M
articles.abstract:
Background: Online Dating Violence (ODV) is increasingly recognized as a distinct form of intimate partner violence, characterized by the use of digital tools to perpetrate control, harassment, or emotional and sexual coercion within romantic relationships. The current aims at Mapping the Global literature in the field of Online Dating Violence by looking at it in the lens of Bibliometric Science. 
Methodology: The Study used Scopus Database to Conduct the Bibliometric Analysis. Initially, 62576 Documents were retrieved from the database, using systematic Bibliometric Approach. The title focused search was performed. Finally, 352 documents were obtained for the Bibliometric Analysis. To conduct the analysis, R software, VOSViewer, Microsoft excel software were utilised. 
Results: The Results found out that western Countries have more publications than the east, especially the United States and United Kingdom are two Influential countries in the field of research on Online dating violence.

articles.title: Working Alone? Working from Home and Political Participation
articles.authors: Erick Stivens Padilla-Galviz
articles.abstract: What are the political consequences of working from home? I study this question in the European context, asking how remote work impacts electoral participation. I test two competing theoretical frameworks: the resource model and the workplace socialisation theory. The resource model suggests that remote work fosters political participation by increasing individuals’ time and civic skills. In contrast, the socialisation hypothesis argues that WFH reduces social interaction and exposure to diverse viewpoints at the workplace, thereby weakening electoral participation. Evidence from cross-country survey data and a causal analysis using Dutch data indicates that WFH reduces electoral participation, with effects that intensify with longer exposure. These effects are driven by diminished exposure to political discussion among work colleagues, supporting the workplace socialisation hypothesis. This study contributes to research on technological change, political socialisation, and the broader societal consequences of remote work, while underscoring the importance of considering democratic implications in the design of future work arrangement policies.

articles.title: The Advantages of Using Bayesian Statistics for Fairness Assessments in Artificial Intelligence Audits
articles.authors: Federica Picogna; Koen Derks; jacques de swart; ruud wetzels
articles.abstract: Artificial Intelligence (AI) is increasingly shaping decision-making in our society, and directly affecting people’s lives. While its use can enhance efficiency, it may also amplify existing biases and adversely affect certain social groups, with potential discriminatory effects. To reduce possible discrimination risk, AI fairness audits grounded in statistical hypothesis testing are crucial. In practice, auditors predominantly rely on tests grounded in the frequentist paradigm. However, standard frequentist null hypothesis significance tests do not directly quantify evidence in favor of fairness, and naïve repeated testing as data accumulate can invalidate fixed-sample \textit{p}-value interpretations unless specialized sequential procedures are used. We argue that Bayesian hypothesis testing provides a more transparent and robust framework for fairness assessment of AI systems with binary outcomes. We illustrate its application through two common audit scenarios: one in which a predefined direction of potential discrimination is specified—i.e., a normative identification of an unprivileged group relative to a privileged one—and another in which no such distinction is made. In the latter scenario, due to the absence of a direction of discrimination, we propose evaluating whether observed differences between groups fall within a predetermined range of tolerable differences, thereby providing a more realistic and practically meaningful framework for assessing fairness.

articles.title: Monitor Digitale Arbeitsgesellschaft – Kurzbericht der vierten Befragungswelle: KI durchdringt zunehmend den Arbeitsalltag: Steigende Nutzung, größere Handlungsspielräume und wachsende Sorgen
articles.authors: Frank Marcinkowski; Birte Keller; Marco Lünich; Florian Golo Flaßhoff
articles.abstract: Der Kurzbericht präsentiert zentrale Ergebnisse der letzten von vier repräsentativen Befragungswellen der Studie Monitors Digitale Arbeitsgesellschaft, die im Rahmen des Forschungsprojekts Meinungsmonitor Künstliche Intelligenz 3.0 durchgeführt wurde. Grundlage sind die Angaben von 1.607 Befragten (915 Erwerbstätige, 692 Nichterwerbstätige) im Juli 2026. Zum Abschluss der Befragungsreihe zeigt sich, dass das Interesse an KI nach dem zwischenzeitlichen Rückgang wieder auf das erhöhte Niveau vom Sommer 2025 steigt, während die subjektive Einschätzung des eigenen Wissens auf einem gegenüber der ersten Erhebung höheren Niveau stabil bleibt. Gleichzeitig fällt die Bewertung der gesellschaftlichen Folgen von KI kritischer aus: Weniger Befragte sehen mehr Nutzen als Risiken, während risikobetonte und ambivalente Einschätzungen zunehmen. In der Arbeitswelt bleibt die Nutzen-Risiko-Bewertung für den eigenen Beruf stabil und leicht nutzenorientiert. Die Einschätzung konkreter Arbeitsbedingungen entwickelt sich teilweise positiver, zugleich nimmt die persönliche Jobunsicherheit erkennbar zu. Besonders deutlich steigt die berufliche KI-Nutzung, die den höchsten Stand der Befragungsreihe erreicht. Zuwächse zeigen sich vor allem bei generativen, empfehlenden, analytischen und entscheidungsnahen Funktionen. Zugleich berichten Beschäftigte häufiger von Nutzungsfreiheit, eigener Entscheidungshoheit und Mitgestaltungsmöglichkeiten, auch wenn die Mehrheit weiterhin keinen Einfluss auf die Einführung von KI am Arbeitsplatz hat. Insgesamt deuten die Ergebnisse auf eine fortschreitende Normalisierung von KI hin: Mit ihrer stärkeren Verbreitung werden sowohl konkrete Vorteile und Handlungsspielräume als auch mögliche Risiken für Beschäftigung und Gesellschaft sichtbarer und differenzierter bewertet.

articles.title: Effects of political polarization on non-electoral participation
articles.authors: Marta Kołczyńska
articles.abstract: Several studies have examined the effects of polarization on election turnout, but the consequences for other forms of participation have remained unexplored. I draw on research on the mechanisms mobilizing non-electoral participation to examine the effects of change in polarization on this form of political engagement, distinguishing institutional and noninstitutional participation. Building on the literatures on respective determinants of both types of participation, I expect polarization to have a positive effect on both types of participation, but I expect that the effect is stronger in the case of noninstitutional polarization. I present longitudinal analyses of the effect of system-level affective and ideological polarization on non-electoral participation as well as protest mobilization in 22 European countries in the period 2002-2019. Results point to a positive effect of polarization on protest participation and mobilization, but show no evidence of an effect of polarization on institutional participation.

articles.title: Open Science is an Urgent Necessity in All Areas of Sociology including Public Sociology
articles.authors: Nate Breznau
articles.abstract: This is a comment on the vision statement for sociology published by Aksoy, Manzo, Birkelund and Raub (2026). It supports their vision of open science in sociology but argues that open science is urgent and should be the first, if not only priority of modern sociology. It discusses recent evidence that sociology is the least reliable of the major social and behavioral science disciplines. It is essentially unreliable as a whole. It also argues that public sociology should not be removed from sociology but simply made transparent and open. Finally, it concludes that sociologists themselves should be humble and honest in public that their discipline is not reliable, rather than defending a failed status quo.

articles.title: SOBRE LA LÓGICA DE CONVERSIÓN DE VOTOS EN ASIENTOS
articles.authors: RICARDO DE LA PEÑA MENA
articles.abstract: Este ensayo examina el proceso de conversión de votos en asientos en las asambleas nacionales, utilizando datos de elecciones en todo el mundo. Analiza la asimetría y desproporcionalidad entre el porcentaje de sufragios que reciben los partidos y las cuotas de poder que obtienen en el legislativo. Para medir este fenómeno, el estudio revisa diversos indicadores basados en la distancia de Minkowski, como los índices de Loosemore-Hanby y de Gallagher, así como modelos teóricos y métricas de fragmentación. Entre sus hallazgos, destaca que los sistemas de representación proporcional generan mayor equidad en la asignación, mientras que los esquemas de mayoría relativa incrementan la desproporcionalidad. Asimismo, se observa que la distorsión tiende a reducirse conforme aumenta el número de contendientes y que los efectos de conversión han mostrado estabilidad a lo largo del siglo XXI, aunque con marcadas disparidades entre regiones geopolíticas.

articles.title: “Ascending dragon or blasting the dragon vein?”: How Chinese netizens construct environmental meanings in digital publics
articles.authors: Yingnian Tao; Mark Ryan
articles.abstract: Corporations’ sustainability communication is increasingly challenged by digital publics. Yet research on how netizens contest corporate sustainability narratives, and thereby construct environmental meanings, remains largely confined to Western contexts. This study addresses this gap by examining Chinese netizens’ discursive responses to a controversial fireworks display in the Himalayas staged by international mountaineering brand Arc’teryx. Comments from the seven most popular Weibo posts were selected to compile a corpus (140,584 tokens),  and analysed through corpus-assisted discourse analysis, particularly keyword and concordance analysis. Findings show that netizens mobilise multiple meaning systems to express strong disapproval, including scientific ecological knowledge, perceptions of environmental governance failure, spiritual-cultural references, consumer action, and nationalism. These interconnected meaning systems converge around a distinctive feature of Chinese digital environmentalism: a nature-centred view of human-nature relations and harmony. The study extends understanding of digital environmentalism beyond Western contexts by showing that environmental meanings in Chinese digital spaces are place- and culture-based, intertwining ecological concerns with emotion, spiritual wellbeing, perceptions of justice, and national interests.

articles.title: EXACTITUD DE LAS ENCUESTAS PREVIAS A LAS ELECCIONES PARA GUBERNATURAS EN MÉXICO, 2024
articles.authors: RICARDO DE LA PEÑA MENA
articles.abstract: El documento analiza la exactitud de 160 encuestas preelectorales publicadas antes de las elecciones para gubernaturas en México en 2024. Para ello, propone metodologías alternativas a las tradicionales de Mosteller, como es la distancia rectilínea basada en las distancias de Minkowski, con el fin de medir de manera más precisa la discrepancia entre las estimaciones demoscópicas y los resultados oficiales de los cómputos.  Entre sus hallazgos principales, el texto destaca que la transición hacia métodos de aproximación no presenciales (como llamadas telefónicas automatizadas y sondeos digitales), impulsada por factores de costo y rapidez, ha disminuido la calidad y capacidad predictiva de los estudios. Asimismo, demuestra que la exactitud de las encuestas está fuertemente determinada por el nivel de competitividad de la contienda: las mediciones tienden a ser más precisas en elecciones altamente competidas, lo cual se evalúa mediante el índice del número efectivo de partidos.

articles.title: MÉXICO 2024: UNA VISIÓN NACIONAL
articles.authors: RICARDO DE LA PEÑA MENA
articles.abstract: El documento analiza los resultados de las elecciones presidenciales en México de 2018 y 2024 utilizando un marco estadístico y comparativo. Examina la evolución de la participación ciudadana, la fragmentación del voto, el número efectivo de partidos y el margen de victoria tanto por partidos políticos como por coaliciones y candidaturas. Su propósito central es superar el análisis casuístico tradicional para construir indicadores y modelos que expliquen la modificación de las preferencias del electorado mexicano y la continuidad o alternancia en el poder.

articles.title: Self-Constructed Recovery from Cognitive Collapse: A retrospective autoethnography
articles.authors: Xin Sun
articles.abstract: Severe childhood maltreatment is known to impair brain development. However, this retrospective single-case autoethnography illustrates that an individual with extreme developmental trauma can achieve functional recovery without formal intervention. This study covers the participant’s life from birth to age 28, and the core recovery period begins with cognitive collapse at age 14 and ends with high functional recovery at age 28. This recovery is marked by the participant‑researcher’s ability to produce academic writing and integrate cross‑disciplinary theories (e.g., active inference) while preparing this manuscript. Consequently, this case introduces a concept of “trauma-type twice‑exceptionality”: a pattern in which extreme developmental trauma co‑occurs with high cognitive reserve, shaping a distinct recovery trajectory that existing models do not capture.

articles.title: Changing governments, stable elites? Executive personnel continuity in global perspective
articles.authors: Marco Improta
articles.abstract: In political science, government change is typically understood as a shift in who holds power, even though new cabinets may formally include many members of the previous governing elite. In this study, I differentiate institutional turnover from personnel turnover by reconstructing transitions between successive governments using the WhoGov dataset. I introduce an Executive Personnel Continuity Index (EPCI) that measures the similarity between outgoing and incoming ministerial rosters. I argue that leader succession functions as an executive reset: new leaders have incentives to establish control, reward loyalists, and signal political change. Party organizations, however, can insulate incumbent ministers from replacement. I test these expectations using descriptive evidence, country and transition-year fixed effects, equal-country weighting, entropy balancing and a transition-centered comparison with the outgoing government's own pre-transition continuity. Across the principal specifications, leader replacement is associated with a decline of approximately one-third in executive personnel continuity. The decline is limited under same-party succession, substantially larger across party boundaries and greatest under complete partisan alternation. The findings therefore indicate that a change in government translates into a substantive transformation of the elite mainly when it also unsettles the leadership and party bases of executive power, and this has significant consequences for political systems worldwide.

articles.title: LA PERCEPCIÓN DE INTEGRIDAD EN LAS MÁS RECIENTES ELECCIONES PARA GUBERNATURAS EN MÉXICO (2021-2024)
articles.authors: RICARDO DE LA PEÑA MENA
articles.abstract: El objetivo central de este ensayo es analizar los datos empíricos disponibles sobre la percepción de la integridad en las elecciones más recientes para las gubernaturas en México, correspondientes al período 2021-2024, y su relación con indicadores directamente vinculados con estos comicios y sus resultados. 	Para ello, se recurre a la información puesta a disposición pública por la Facultad Latinoamericana de Ciencias Sociales (FLACSO) México como Proyecto de integridad electoral subnacional en México 2015-2024 y accesible en Harvard Dataverse (Loza et al., 2025), seleccionando los datos relativos a las elecciones de gubernaturas más recientes en cada una de las 32 entidades federativas de México. 	Del análisis realizado se concluye que, al menos con los datos analizados,  no existe alguna variable vinculada con los resultados electorales que explique claramente las diferencias en las percepciones de integridad electoral que han sido compiladas.

articles.title: Before You Diagnose Her: AI Companionship as Structural Question, Not Symptom
articles.authors: Mingzhu Liu
articles.abstract: AI companionship is surging worldwide, and research on the phenomenon has grown exponentially. However, across the research literature tracking it, from human-computer interaction to communication and the social sciences, a shared pathologizing tendency and its attendant alarmism have set in. This essay argues that the diagnosis has outrun its evidence. The harm literature leans on extreme cases and habitual slippery-slope leaps; it systematically conflates three distinct propositions: that AI companions cause harm, that particular platform designs amplify harm, and that AI companionship as an intimate practice is inherently pathological. The essay further deconstructs the philosophical underpinnings of this pathologizing stance, showing how its ontological assumptions rely on a foreclosed definition of relation. Crucially, such frameworks rarely ask what users' human relationships and social circumstances were before they arrived. Drawing on preliminary observations of Chinese-language public discourse — a field that, over sustained observation, has been almost uniformly female — this essay documents user practices that the deficit frame cannot accommodate — building, theorizing, ethical deliberation, and the organized refusal of the clinical gaze. Connecting these user practices to a longer tradition of female emotional workarounds from romance narratives to fan cultures as exits from inequitable intimate arrangements, I propose structural emotional refuge as an alternative unit of analysis: AI companionship understood as a rational emotional migration from arrangements that extract more than they return. The essay does not answer one totalizing diagnosis with another; it argues for conceptual restraint until the evidence arrives, and for asking where users came from, why they left, and how they understand themselves before writing the answer as psychological problems.

articles.title: METODOLOGÍA PARA EL ANÁLISIS DE LOS CAMBIOS EN EL SISTEMA DE REPRESENTACIÓN DE LAS CÁMARAS BAJAS DEL MUNDO (1995-2025)
articles.authors: RICARDO DE LA PEÑA MENA
articles.abstract: Este ensayo analiza el impacto de las reformas en los sistemas de representación de las cámaras bajas del mundo entre 1995 y 2025, utilizando datos de Varieties of Democracy (V-Dem). Partiendo de una metodología original basada en una base de datos propia, se examinan las variaciones en el voto del partido mayor, el margen de victoria y el número efectivo de partidos tras modificaciones institucionales como la magnitud del distrito, umbrales y fórmulas de asignación. Los hallazgos empíricos revelan que, contrariamente a las expectativas de la ingeniería constitucional clásica, las consecuencias inmediatas de dichas reformas sobre el reparto de votos son marginales y compensatorias, sugiriendo que actúan más como elementos estabilizadores que como factores de transformación radical del comportamiento electoral.

articles.title: From Flagship to Firm: Gatekeeping, Employer Sorting, and the Returns to College
articles.authors: Aleksei Opacic
articles.abstract: Firms increasingly drive college graduates' labor market earnings, yet the vast literature on the value-added of college has largely overlooked their role. Drawing on human capital theory and institutional theories of credentialism, closure, and organizational matching, I argue that college-to-workplace pipelines are a critical driver of college value-added. To test this, I assemble a novel US employer-employee matched dataset merged with postsecondary and high school academic records. Firm placement explains much of the variation in earnings premiums between colleges. Absent firm sorting, the range of counterfactual earnings differences across colleges would fall by 56%, and over half of the earnings advantage to attending the state flagship comes from access to higher-paying employers. These sorting effects extend broadly across the distribution of high-wage firms, and not merely a handful of elite employers. Crucially, sorting effects do not simply reflect skill-based advantages, implying that college quality derives as much from institutional linkages to the labor market as from human capital development. Policies aimed at broadening recruitment pipelines, rather than solely improving instructional inputs, are therefore essential to reducing inequalities in the economic returns to higher education.

articles.title: Open University of Nepal initiative: Lessons learned from designing an institution of higher learning
articles.authors: Pramod Dhakal; Drona Rasali; Ambika P. Adhikari; Raju Adhikari
articles.abstract:
A group of Nepali diaspora members, represented by the Non-Resident Nepali Association (NRNA), started a campaign in 2009 to establish the Open University of Nepal (OUN) in partnership with the government of Nepal. Their motivation was to develop a quality university for the masses by mobilizing local, diaspora, and international collaborators for producing and disseminating knowledge in the public domain. The university was subsequently established in 2017, but it drifted away from many of the original objectives. Most critically, it embraced distance
education as its central function while setting aside the aspiration of producing and sharing knowledge in the public domain. As the original proponents of this mission, the authors share their experiences and lessons learned so that other campaigners of similar institution-building missions could benefit.

articles.title: Evaluation of Development Communication Strategies Employed in the Promotion and Sustainability of Environmental Campaigns in Edo State
articles.authors: Adriel Ekozin; Bobby Eghosa Obayuwana; Gloria Ehimwema Ogono
articles.abstract: The study titled Evaluation of Development Communication Strategies Employed in the Promotion and Sustainability of Environmental Campaigns in Edo State examined how communication strategies influence environmental awareness, participation, and behavioural change among residents in Edo State. The main objective was to evaluate the communication strategies employed in promoting environmental campaigns in Edo State, and the level of audience participation and engagement. Guided by the Development Communication Theory, which emphasises participatory and dialogic communication as drivers of social transformation, the study adopted a survey research design. A sample size of 400 was determined from a population of 5.1 million residents using the Taro Yamane formula. Data were gathered through a structured questionnaire administered to respondents purposively selected based on their exposure to environmental campaigns. Descriptive statistics, including mean and standard deviation, were used for analysis, with a benchmark of 3.00 for acceptance. Findings revealed that development communication strategies such as radio, television, and social media are highly effective tools for environmental advocacy, with social media emerging as the dominant platform. However, campaigns conducted in local languages were less frequent, indicating a gap in linguistic inclusivity. Respondents generally perceived campaign messages as clear and persuasive, though some noted that technical language limited understanding. The results further showed that while awareness and attitudinal changes have improved, tangible environmental outcomes, such as reduced pollution and cleaner surroundings, remain minimal due to weak community participation and limited follow-up mechanisms. The study concluded that although development communication has significantly increased environmental awareness in Edo State, its impact on sustained behavioural change is still limited by inadequate grassroots involvement and inconsistent message localisation. It recommended that environmental campaigns should strengthen community-based collaborations, adopt culturally relevant and localised communication approaches, and integrate environmental education into school curricula to foster long-term eco-consciousness.

articles.title: Performance Measures and Mean-Variance Efficiency
articles.authors: Woongki Lee
articles.abstract: While portfolio performance and pricing performance are often treated as separate domains, both rest on the same foundation: mean-variance efficiency. This study makes that connection explicit by examining 11 performance measures drawn from these two domains. We show that these measures share a common basis in the Sharpe ratio, the standard measure of mean-variance efficiency, and can therefore be interpreted within a unified framework. Building on this result, we derive two compact benchmark-relative metrics, the ratio metric and the gap metric, and illustrate their practical relevance using data from the Korean fund industry.

articles.title: Fund Manager Alpha in Tactical Asset Allocation
articles.authors: Woongki Lee
articles.abstract: This study focuses on the stock picking dimension of tactical asset allocation. To reflect the fact that each manager’s opportunity set is constrained by the fund’s style, we construct a style-matching portfolio and use it to define manager alpha as a time-varying measure of stock picking ability. We then distinguish between this full time-varying measure of manager alpha and the portion left unexplained by factor exposures. The former captures ordinary stock picking ability, whereas the latter captures superior stock picking ability. This distinction forms the basis of our empirical analysis of stock picking ability in the Korean fund industry.

articles.title: Exigência de Inglês “para Inglês ver”: Exclusão Antecipatória na Transição para o Mercado de Trabalho entre Graduados Cotistas
articles.authors: Omar Koshin; Andre Vieira
articles.abstract:
Resumo

Este artigo examina o papel da exigência de fluência em inglês nos processos de contratação de graduados e sua contribuição para a reprodução de desigualdades sociais e raciais no mercado de trabalho brasileiro. Os dados provêm de 19 entrevistas semiestruturadas realizadas no Rio de Janeiro e em São Paulo entre julho de 2025 e janeiro de 2026: 18 com graduados beneficiários da política de cotas em universidades federais e uma com um consultor de contratação de diversidade. O argumento central é que, nos contextos analisados, a exigência de fluência em inglês pode operar como um mecanismo de fechamento social na transição entre a conclusão da educação superior e o acesso ao emprego. Esse mecanismo se estrutura por três processos inter-relacionados: (i) triagem por um recurso cultural cuja aquisição é fortemente estratificada por classe e raça; (ii) legitimação institucional do requisito como marcador de profissionalismo, mesmo quando sua relevância funcional para as atividades desempenhadas é limitada; e (iii) exclusão antecipatória de candidatos que, ao se depararem com a exigência, deixam de disputar determinadas vagas. Os resultados mostram ainda um descompasso recorrente entre o nível de proficiência formalmente exigido, sua avaliação nos processos seletivos e o uso efetivo do idioma no trabalho, sugerindo que o requisito pode produzir efeitos seletivos antes mesmo da seleção formal.

Palavras-chave: desigualdades raciais; mercado de trabalho; estratificação; educação superior; ação afirmativa

articles.title: Thematic clusters and emotions on x during Ecuador’s 2024 blackouts
articles.authors: Oscar Molina-Bailon; Juan Ignacio Revestido; Antonia Ramírez-García; Jorge Márquez López
articles.abstract: This study characterizes the conversation on the social network X during the prolonged blackouts that Ecuador endured in late 2024. For this purpose, 3,952 posts published between September and December were analyzed. The messages were grouped by semantic proximity, classified into affective-communicative categories, and their stability was verified; the daily composition was contrasted with the scheduled outage hours using models that respect the interdependence of proportions. The corpus was organized into four discursive functions—psychosocial distress, media framing, informational monitoring, and politicization—each with its own affective profile and shifting presence.
