The grouping proved consistent throughout the procedure. These profiles broaden the information offered by aggregate polarity and provide useful criteria for the field of crisis communication.

articles.title: Effects of Cost Control Techniques on the Profitability of Listed Manufacturing Companies in Nigeria
articles.authors: Adriel Ekozin; Franklin Taiye Umaigba; Michael Jimoh Amedu; Doris Esohe Aiworo; Richard Usengbuwa; Ruth Abieyuwa Uhunamure; Endurance Izokun
articles.abstract: The profitability of Nigerian manufacturing firms has come under sustained pressure from rising material, energy and overhead costs, currency volatility and intense competition, prompting renewed interest in cost control as a controllable lever of financial performance. This study examined the effect of cost control techniques on the profitability of listed manufacturing companies in Nigeria, disaggregating cost control into material cost control (MCC), labour cost control (LCC) and overhead cost control (OCC). Grounded in the Contingency Theory of Management Accounting and the Theory of Economies of Scale, the study adopted an ex-post facto design using a balanced panel of ten listed manufacturing firms over the ten-year period 2015-2024 (100 firm-year observations). Data extracted from audited financial statements were analysed using descriptive statistics, Pearson correlation and fixed-effects panel regression, with firm size and leverage as control variables and return on assets (ROA) and net profit margin (NPM) as measures of profitability. The three cost-control dimensions jointly explain approximately 57% of the variation in profitability (adjusted R² = 0.571; F = 27.4, p < .001). The results confirm that the systematic control of costs especially material and overhead costs is a significant driver of manufacturing profitability, corroborating recent Nigerian panel evidence. The study concluded that cost control techniques significantly affect the profitability of listed manufacturing companies in Nigeria over 2015-2024 and recommended prioritising material- and overhead-cost control, institutionalising budgetary control and standard costing and adopting contemporary tools such as activity-based costing and lean manufacturing.

articles.title: Collective Sexuality Frames as Unambiguous Settings: Event Descriptions and Participant Reactions in Germany
articles.authors: Oliver Maor
articles.abstract: This exploratory study examines organized sexual events in Germany as structured leisure formats rather than as expressions of identity, morality, or relationship ideology. Using event descriptions, registration data, pricing information, and post-event participant comments published on a dominant German online platform, the analysis shifts attention from individual motivations to recurrent organizational configurations through which sexual practices are enabled. The dataset comprises 137 publicly advertised events conducted on three comparable Saturdays in late summer and fall 2025, enabling comparison with a prior 2023 sample. Quantitative analyses show that admission pricing, including gender-differentiated prices and age-related discounts, has no measurable effect on participant composition. Multivariate analyses identified four largely independent structural dimensions—demographic composition, participation structure, pricing relations by gender, and absolute pricing—and a three-cluster typology distinguishing large party-oriented events, couple-centered standard formats, and niche events with a large surplus of men. No evidence of a stable participant cohort across years is found. Qualitative analyses of event descriptions and participant comments indicate that sexuality is treated as a situational and pragmatic practice. Evaluations of events in the participants’ comments focus primarily on organizational coherence, spatial layout, music, catering, and staff performance. Sexual encounters are mentioned selectively, mainly where organizers explicitly curate sexual practices as part of the event design. Overall, the findings suggest that organized sexual events operate as bounded social settings in which the event format defines the purpose of participation, allowing sexuality to be enacted as a routinized form of leisure activity embedded in the spatial and service setting.

articles.title: Views of Owan West Local Government Residents on the Socio-Cultural Impact of Childlessness on Married Couples
articles.authors: Adriel Ekozin; Johnson Oamien Okaigbuan; Godsent Onobhen Ibhate
articles.abstract: In many African societies, marriage is expected to lead to child bearing and perpetuation of the family and childlessness is a significant reproductive health and social welfare issue. These experiences of stigma, discrimination, psychological distress, marital instability and socio-economic exclusion are common for married couples in Nigeria who experience involuntary childlessness. Although, there has been massive focus on the socio-cultural implications of infertility and reproductive health issues among married couples, there is a dearth of empirical studies on the same in Owan West Local Government Area, Edo State. In this study, the socio-cultural effects of childlessness on married couples were explored focusing on the causes of childlessness and the socio-cultural effects experienced by affected married couples. The study revealed that the childless couples suffer from serious social stigma, emotional trauma, family pressure, marital problems, humiliation, isolation and economic difficulties as a result of the cultural norms associated with marriage and child bearing. Women were also determined to be at a higher risk of being blamed regardless of the medical reason for the infertility. The findings showed that childlessness is not only a medical condition but also a serious socio-cultural problem that impacts on the wellbeing and quality of life of married couples. It suggested raising public awareness, expanding access to reproductive health services, psychosocial support programmes and community-based initiatives to combat discriminatory cultural practices, as well as strengthening social work interventions to mitigate the stigma and foster inclusive family support systems.

articles.title: Natural disasters and the two dimensions of redistributive demands: evidence from a major earthquake
articles.authors: Irene Pañeda-Fernández
articles.abstract: Whether natural hazards raise redistributive demands remains poorly understood. I argue that the distinction between taking from the rich and giving to the poor is essential to understand the impact of disasters. I expect natural disasters to not spark demands to “soak the rich” because their unfair advantage is less visible than is the case after other economic shocks. I theorize natural hazards raise demands to redistribute to the poor because these events force close experiences with socio-economic others. Combining variation in exposure to Japan’s 2011 devastating earthquake with representative panel data, results are consistent with my propositions. Even though beliefs in the role of luck increased across the board, demands to redistribute from the rich decreased after the disaster and demands for pro-poor redistribution increased in affected areas. These findings set natural hazards apart from other types of economic shocks such as job loss, financial crises, or mass warfare.

articles.title: Arts-Based Storytelling in Science Dissemination and Knowledge Generation: Diverse Perspectives in and about Digital Society
articles.authors: Bieke Zaman; Priscilla Van Even; Jonas Rutgeerts
articles.abstract: Digital transformation is reshaping how scientific knowledge is produced, circulated, and imagined. Yet this shift also amplifies concerns about epistemic narrowing, as digitally mediated, AI driven discourses consolidate dominant narratives and reinforce cultural imperialism. This chapter proposes arts‑based storytelling as a potential response. On the one hand, we discuss the potential of arts-based storytelling as a form of science communication different from the typical one-directional dissemination. On the other hand, we examine arts-based storytelling as a speculative practice of creative imagination and knowledge generation through fabulation. Both practices share similar epistemic and democratic potential: they both set out to construct publics through inclusive forms of engagement and leverage the potential of creative modes of expression to foster plural ways of knowing and challenge hegemonic narratives. The chapter does not consider arts-based storytelling as a universal or flawless approach. We posit it as a complementary epistemic practice that becomes meaningful if practiced in an inclusive way with critical reflexivity towards its own situated nature, which is inevitably entangled with the very systems it seeks to challenge. Embracing this situatedness allows us to view arts‑based storytelling as a continuous negotiation of epistemic inclusion in a digital era.

articles.title: Election Campaigns
articles.authors: Florian Foos; Lennard Metson
articles.abstract: In this chapter we explore the political science of election campaigns. We begin with the puzzle that originally motivated the study of campaigns: whether campaigns matter for explaining electoral behaviour. We then outline findings on the specific effects that campaigns have on turnout, vote choice, and mobilising activists. After this, we explore the implications that advances in technology have had in the development of data-driven campaigning. We conclude the chapter with a discussion of key methodological approaches and ethical considerations when studying campaigns.

articles.title: Perception of Radio Portrayal of Disability among People Living with Disabilities in Ilorin, Kwara State
articles.authors: Adriel Ekozin; Victor Olusegun Babatunde; Oluwajuwonlo Emmanuel Ayanwale
articles.abstract: This study investigated the perspectives of People with Disabilities (PWDs) in Ilorin on radio representation of disability, particularly the radio programmes. A qualitative research design was adopted, using Key Informant Interviews to gather in-depth insights from 15 visually impaired persons in Ilorin. Media Representation Theory was used as an anchor for this study, which focused on how PWDs perceive the representation of disability in radio reports, the prevalent themes and frames in radio coverage, and the consequences of such representation for social inclusion and identity. Findings showed that there is significant improvement regarding the representation of PWDs in media, and in particular in the use of more inclusive themes, frames, and images. While the study did not focus on a particular radio programme but explored the various programmes the informants listen to, it also found that most radio programmes targeted at PWDs are anchored and promoted by PWDs themselves, while programmes handled by non-PWDs often fail to adequately reflect the lived realities of persons with disabilities. However, some non-PWD broadcasters with training in special education were considered more sensitive in their coverage. Despite the progress recorded, informants noted that awareness and representation of disability issues on the radio remain limited. The study finds that although radio has become more inclusive, there is a gap in disability awareness, inclusion of PWD voices, and disability portrayals that can promote social inclusion and minimise stereotypes in society.

articles.title: Measuring Meaning on Video at Scale, from classifier to theory interpreter: From Classifier to Theory Interpreter in AI-Based Humor Annotation
articles.authors: YAMAUCHI SHIMMEI
articles.abstract:
The rapid development of generative artificial intelligence (AI), particularly large
language models (LLMs), has created new opportunities for measuring complex and
culturally embedded phenomena. However, existing applications largely focus on textbased
data and predefined classification tasks, leaving multimodal and interactional
phenomena underexplored.
This study proposes a framework for analyzing humor in video data by introducing
humor events as the unit of analysis, defined as temporally bounded sequences linking
an utterance, its multimodal delivery, and audience laughter. Using a large corpus of
Saturday Night Live (SNL) clips, we extract and classify 5,690 humor events with a
multimodal generative AI model. To examine how AI can annotate complex cultural
phenomena, we compare three prompt strategies: a definition-based prompt, an
interaction-oriented prompt, and a theory-informed prompt grounded in sociological
theories of humor. Results show that the theory-informed prompt substantially improves
performance, particularly for categories requiring contextual and multimodal
interpretation. Beyond performance, the study demonstrates that prompt design
systematically shapes how cultural phenomena are measured. While aggregate category
distributions remain stable across prompts, label assignments at the event level vary in
structured ways, indicating that prompts function as measurement frames rather than
neutral instructions.
The study makes three main contributions. First, it introduces an interactional and
multimodal unit of analysis for video-based research, providing a concrete approach to
operationalizing meaning in context. Second, it reconceptualizes generative AI not
merely as a classifier but as a theory interpreter, capable of operationalizing sociological
concepts when guided by theoretical prompts. Third, it shows that prompts themselves
constitute measurement frameworks, suggesting that prompt design should be treated as
an object of methodological scrutiny—potentially subject to evaluation and review in its
own right. More broadly, the findings highlight that cultural phenomena are both
structurally patterned and interpretively open, and that AI-based measurement
inevitably reflects the analytical frames embedded in prompt design. Although
annotating complex cultural phenomena remains challenging, the results suggest that
generative AI offers a viable and scalable approach for video-based analysis when
guided by explicit category definitions and theoretically informed prompts, providing a
significant methodological advance over existing approaches

articles.title: Fund Manager Beta in Tactical Asset Allocation
articles.authors: Woongki Lee
articles.abstract: We show that realized returns are shaped by two opposing intertemporal forces. They rise with expected short-term returns but fall when risk subsequently increases. Successful timing therefore requires attention not only to favorable return expectations but also to future risk. This logic leads to a two-component specification of manager beta. One raises exposure when near-term opportunities are favorable, while the other lowers exposure when future risk is expected to rise. Market timing is thus represented as a tactical adjustment of portfolio exposure that seeks gains while limiting losses from subsequent risk increases.

articles.title: Gendered Adoption of Generative Artificial Intelligence among Gen Z Social Media Influencers in Malaysia’s Content Creation Industry: Intellectual Property Challenges and Ethical Imperatives
articles.authors: SF Syed Abdul Rahman
articles.abstract: This conceptual review examines gender differences in the adoption of generative artificial intelligence (GenAI) by Generation Z (Gen Z) social media influencers and content creators operating online businesses in Malaysia. Drawing on recent empirical and policy evidence from 2025–2026, it analyses how male and female Gen Z creators differentially integrate AI tools into content production, audience engagement, and monetisation strategies within Malaysia’s rapidly expanding creator economy and high social-media penetration environment (Telenor Asia, 2025). Parallel attention is given to emerging intellectual property (IP) ambiguities surrounding AI-assisted and AI-generated content, alongside ethical concerns including authenticity, disclosure obligations, deepfake risks, cultural representation, and algorithmic bias. Findings synthesised from contemporary studies indicate functional differentiation rather than simple access gaps: male creators more frequently employ AI for technical and coding-oriented tasks, while female creators concentrate on text generation, creative writing, and aesthetic enhancement (Raza et al., 2026). Persistent gendered risk perceptions regarding societal harms further moderate adoption intensity, particularly among younger women (Stephany & Duszynski, 2026). Malaysia’s human-centred copyright framework under the Copyright Act 1987 leaves significant gaps for AI-generated works, exposing creators, especially those building personal brands, to ownership uncertainty and unauthorised replication of likeness or style (Wardi et al., 2025). The paper proposes an integrated ethical-governance and IP-reform agenda tailored to the Malaysian creator ecosystem and calls for gender-responsive AI literacy programmes, mandatory disclosure standards, and updated guidance from the Malaysian Intellectual Property Organisation (MyIPO). Implications for policy, platform design, and future empirical research are discussed.

articles.title: Dual Exposure: Systematic and Systemic Risk
articles.authors: Woongki Lee
articles.abstract: Systemic risk can be measured by the covariance between an institution’s return and the sector return. This allows systemic risk to be decomposed by decomposing the sector return. When the sector return is separated into a market-driven component and a market-orthogonal residual, systemic risk splits into systematic risk, reflecting exposure to the market-driven component, and net systemic risk, reflecting exposure to the residual. We examine how these two risk dimensions relate to financial sector returns, contemporaneously and intertemporally. Using a sample including the 2008 global financial crisis, we find that including both risks explains substantial variation in financial sector returns.

articles.title: Ethical Challenges of Gamification in Healthcare and Health Promotion: A Systematic Thematic Analysis
articles.authors: Nooruldeen Taffar
articles.abstract:
Introduction: the concept of gamification provides possible solutions for the field of healthcare in terms of efficiency, and behavioural change. This work is a trial systematically highlighting the ethical considerations of gamification in healthcare. This research analyses the ethical effects of gamification on healthcare and health approach on a systematic basis.

Methodology: the author follows a thematic analysis-based approach to highlight the themes of ethical challenges facing the implementation of gamification in healthcare and health promotion. This paper follows the PRISMA flow diagram for data collection. SPIDER and CASP checklist are used for search strategy and quality appraisal.

Results and discussion: seven different themes of ethical challenges are identified in the literature including harm, privacy, manipulation and exploitation, inequality and stereotypes encouragement, data ownership, merging of the real and the virtual world, and the change of power dynamics. Such themes interact with each other in a thematic way that highlights a cause-and-effect relationship.

Conclusion: the paper provides an interactive framework of ethical challenges scenarios. The author concludes that the use of different search words presented new themes in comparison to the previous work on the topic and the need for further widening of the scope of research for identification of more themes.

articles.title: Artificial Intelligence and the Transformation of the Graphic Design Landscape in Malaysia: Implications for Professional Futures and Higher Education Reform
articles.authors: SF Syed Abdul Rahman
articles.abstract:
The rapid integration of generative artificial intelligence (GenAI) into creative workflows has fundamentally altered the graphic design industry worldwide, with particularly pronounced effects in emerging creative economies such as Malaysia. This article examines how AI technologies have reshaped professional practices, labour dynamics, and creative processes within Malaysia’s graphic design sector. Drawing on recent empirical studies conducted among Malaysian design students and practitioners, the analysis explores efficiency gains, authenticity concerns, cultural representation challenges, and shifts in required competencies (Wong et al., 2025; Artificial Intelligence Integration among Design Students in Malaysia, 2025). Evidence indicates that while GenAI tools accelerate ideation and production, they simultaneously raise questions about originality and the preservation of culturally specific visual languages that characterise Malaysian design practice (Abdullah et al., 2025; Azizi & Sannusi, 2025).
The discussion then addresses the evolving roles of graphic designers, emphasising hybrid human–AI collaboration, conceptual leadership, and cultural fluency as essential future competencies (Zhou et al., 2025; Lestari, 2026). Designers are increasingly required to function as orchestrators of algorithmic outputs rather than sole executors of visual tasks, a shift that demands both technical fluency and critical judgment. Finally, the article evaluates the responsibilities of Malaysian universities in redesigning academic programmes to prepare graduates for an AI-mediated profession. Recommendations include systematic curriculum integration of AI literacy, ethical frameworks, critical design thinking, and industry-aligned experiential learning (Yang, 2025; Bing, 2025). The paper argues that proactive educational reform is essential to ensure that Malaysian designers retain competitive advantage while safeguarding cultural authenticity and professional identity in an increasingly automated creative landscape.

articles.title: Patient Preferences for Non-Opioid Regimens in Chronic Non-Cancer Pain: A Systematic Review of Discrete Choice Experiments
articles.authors: Ni Wayan Mahahari; Kadek Tania Mediana Putri; Ni Putu Aryati Suryaningsih; Gde Palguna Reganata; Dewa Ayu Putu Satrya Dewi; Kadek Hendra Darmawan
articles.abstract: Chronic non-cancer pain is highly prevalent, and concerns about long-term opioid harms have increased interest in non-opioid therapies. Understanding which treatment attributes patients value is essential for shared decision-making. This systematic review synthesised discrete choice experiments (DCEs) to identify the treatment attributes patients prioritise when choosing non-opioid regimens for chronic non-cancer pain, and to appraise the methodological quality of the underlying studies. Following PRISMA 2020 guidance and a prospectively registered protocol (PROSPERO CRD420251273180), we searched nine databases (MEDLINE, Embase, CINAHL, PsycINFO, Scopus, Web of Science, EconLit, PubMed and the Cochrane Library). Two reviewers independently screened records and assessed methodological quality using a modified ISPOR Conjoint Analysis Good Research Practices checklist. Attributes were classified using the Sain et al. (2020) framework into outcome, process and cost categories, and synthesised narratively. Seventeen studies (1,540 records identified) met the inclusion criteria, encompassing 109 attributes; 88% were industry-funded. Outcome attributes predominated (67.9%), followed by process (25.7%) and cost (6.4%). Clinical effectiveness was the most influential attribute, identified as the primary priority in 57.1% of studies combining all three categories, with safety acting as a key differentiator and cost as a constraint. Most studies met ISPOR standards (scores 10.5 to 12), though visual aids (71%) and direct patient input (18%) were underused. Patients prioritise clinical benefit when choosing non-opioid pain therapies, informing preference-sensitive decision-making, clinical guidelines and health technology assessment.

articles.title: EL ILIBERALISMO COMO OPCIÓN ELECTORAL PARTIDARIA EN EL MUNDO (2000-2019)
articles.authors: RICARDO DE LA PEÑA MENA
articles.abstract: En este texto se acude a los datos de la base de datos por partido del proyecto Varieties of Democracy (V-Dem) para el período 2000-2019, utilizando un índice sobre iliberalismo. Del análisis se concluye que la adopción de una actitud iliberal hacia los oponentes responde primordialmente a un posicionamiento en el eje populismo-elitismo, donde lo populista se vincula más comúnmente con lo iliberal, especialmente en el discurso de la derecha. Asumir una posición de ruptura con los principios democrático-liberales resulta claramente redituable en votos y asientos. Esto se refleja en que, mientras sólo el 45% de los partidos liberales participan en gobiernos (menos de una quinta parte como componente mayoritario), el 62% de los partidos con posturas contrarias al respeto a sus contendientes accede al gobierno, siendo el componente mayoritario en más de una tercera parte de las ocasiones.

articles.title: Patient Preferences for Biologic Therapies in Chronic Disease: A Systematic Review of Discrete Choice Experiments
articles.authors: Kadek Tania Mediana Putri; Ni Wayan Mahahari; Dewa Ayu Putu Satrya Dewi; Ni Putu Aryati Suryaningsih; Putu Yudhistira Budi Setiawan; Kadek Hendra Darmawan
articles.abstract:
Introduction: Balancing high efficacy against significant toxicity risks a central challenge in biologic therapy selection for chronic diseases. This systematic review evaluated discrete choice experiments (DCEs) of patient preferences for biologic therapy to identify the treatment attributes that most consistently influence patient choice.
Methods: MEDLINE, Embase, Scopus, CINAHL, and Web of Science were searched (PROSPERO CRD420251271716) for Discrete Choice Experiments (DCEs) evaluating patient preferences for biologic therapies. Two reviewers independently screened eligible studies, extracted study characteristics and treatment attributes, evaluated methodological quality using an ISPOR-based quality assessment instrument, and identified the two most important treatment attributes reported in each study.
Results: Twenty-four studies (2010-2025), most published after 2020, met inclusion criteria across a range of chronic diseases, most frequently psoriasis, rheumatoid arthritis, and inflammatory bowel disease. Of 173 attributes identified, 61% were outcome attributes, 34% process, and 5% cost. Patients most often prioritized the risk of serious adverse events, followed by treatment response; process features gained importance when efficacy and safety differences were minimal, and cost carried greater weight where out-of-pocket expenditure was higher. Twenty-three of 24 studies achieved the maximum ISPOR score of 9/9
Conclusions: Patient preferences in biologic selection follow a clear hierarchy determined by perceived risk, expected benefit, and treatment context. Incorporating these preferences into shared decision-making might improve treatment alignment and long-term patient adherence. This evidence supports patient-centered care and counseling at the initiation of treatment.

articles.title: Political Memes as Participatory Rhetoric for Voter Mobilisation during Elections
articles.authors: Adriel Ekozin; Osa Director Uhunmwenkpenma; Onyeoma Osife-Kurex
articles.abstract: Political communication during elections has increasingly shifted to digital spaces, with political memes emerging as a dominant form of citizen-generated content. This study examined political memes as participatory rhetoric for voter mobilisation during elections in Nigeria. Anchored on Participatory Rhetoric Theory, Framing Theory and Agenda-Setting Theory, the study adopted the library research method. Findings revealed memes framed candidates as “heroes,” “villains” or “incompetent” and such affective frames recorded the highest engagement and correlated significantly with turnout intention. Thematic analysis also showed that viral memes set the agenda for peer political discussion by foregrounding issues such as youth inclusion and insecurity. Thus, the study concluded that political memes function as participatory rhetorical artefacts that simplify electoral issues, foster in-group solidarity and mobilise first-time and apathetic voters beyond elite-controlled campaign channels. However, the circulation of satirical misinformation within memes poses risks to informed participation.

articles.title: AI Incidents and Marginalized Populations: A Descriptive Analysis of the AI Incident Database (1983–2026) from a Social Work Perspective
articles.authors: Nanyi Deng; Sebastian Douglas; Jemel P. Aguilar; Wen Yin
articles.abstract:
Purpose: Artificial intelligence (AI) systems are increasingly deployed in the institutional core of social work practice, such as law enforcement, healthcare, education, and public administration. Despite this implementation, the social work profession lacks a population-level empirical baseline of documented AI-related harm. This study characterizes the landscape of documented AI incidents, focusing on marginalized populations and the sectors in which social workers practice.
Method: We conducted a cross-sectional descriptive analysis of the AI Incident Database (AIID; snapshot as of June 29, 2026), a curated repository of publicly reported AI incidents. The record comprises 1,549 incidents (1983–2026), with three independent post hoc classification systems that provide harm coding for overlapping subsets of these incidents. We report descriptive population proportions with explicit denominators for every reported statistic.
Results: Most incidents (83.8%) were dated 2020 or later, though documented incidents date back to 1983, predating large language models by decades. Among the 214 CSET-coded incidents, a subset weighted toward pre-2020 events, 32.7% involved protected characteristics, most often race or ethnicity. Social-work-relevant sectors, including healthcare, law enforcement, education, and public administration, accounted for 23.4% of these incidents. Incidents in these sectors implicated protected characteristics (50.0% vs. 27.4%) and rights violations (40.0% vs. 4.9%) at markedly higher rates than other sectors, and 80.0% involved the public sector. Among incidents classified by intent and deployment timing, discrimination and toxicity incidents were coded as unintentional in 80.7% of cases, and 97.6% occurred after the AI system was already in active use rather than during development or testing.
Discussion: Documented AI incidents concentrate on the sectors and populations central to social work's mandate. These findings establish an empirical baseline for AI harm surveillance and ground specific advocacy priorities: mandatory incident reporting in publicly funded services, third-party algorithmic auditing, and algorithmic literacy in frontline practice.

articles.title: A scoping review of threats, enabling technologies, and forms of AI involvement associated with child sexual exploitation and abuse
articles.authors: Chad Hemady; Sara Valdebenito; Chanel Hayre; Franziska Meinck; Deborah Fry
articles.abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI) is increasingly implicated in child sexual exploitation and abuse (CSEA), but inconsistent terminology has limited synthesis. This scoping review mapped reported AI-CSEA threats and enabling technologies and examined how AI systems participated in perpetration. English-language sources published from January 2010 to 1 April 2026 were eligible if they concerned children under 18 and where an AI system played a material role in the abuse process. Searches of the ACM Digital Library, CINAHL, Web of Science, EBSCOhost databases, and grey literature identified 48 sources. Three reviewers contributed to screening and data charting, and extracted data were summarised numerically and through qualitative content analysis. Overall, our review found that AI-CSEA nomenclature conflated abusive conduct, production methods and system roles. Five non-exclusive threat domains comprised i) AI-generated CSAM, ii) AI-manipulated CSAM, iii) grooming, iv) sextortion, and v) conversational AI sexual abuse. Six technology groups encompassed: i) generative systems; ii) model adaptation and training data; iii) media manipulation systems; iv) conversational systems; v) immersive and embodied technologies; and vi) access, hosting, and distribution infrastructure. Forms of AI involvement include: i) AI-enabled assistance with person-directed abuse; ii) AI-simulated co-production of user-initiated scenarios; and iii) AI-driven initiation or escalation of sexualised conduct. AI-CSEA largely reflected established forms of abuse reshaped by new modes of production and interaction. Existing act-based classifications of violence against children provide a suitable foundation but require supplementary recording of production route, child linkage, system role and point of steering.

articles.title: Record Linkage Error and Inference in Population Research
articles.authors: Casey Breen; Won-tak Joo
articles.abstract: The explosion in digitization of large-scale administrative data and advances in record linkage have opened up new possibilities for studying core topics in population research, including social mobility, early-life determinants of longevity, and shifts in ethnoracial identity. Much attention has been paid to improving record linkage algorithms, but methodological guidance for researchers analyzing linked data is limited. We propose a general framework to explain how different types of linkage errors—false matches and missed matches—impact inference with linked data and introduce a bias-correction method. We then conduct three empirical case studies on canonical topics in population research: social mobility, the education–longevity gradient, and shifts in ethnoracial identification. These case studies demonstrate the settings in which linkage errors do and do not meaningfully impact substantive research findings. We conclude with practical recommendations for researchers performing inference with linked data and provide an accompanying R package implementing the methods introduced in this paper.

articles.title: How Schools Organize the Standard Life Course and Translate It into Relations to the Self
articles.authors: Vance Byun
articles.abstract:
This paper analyzes why the educational success narrative and standard life-course pathway continue to organize Korean schools despite their uneven efficacy, and how this structure is translated into students' self-relations and differentiated suffering. The educational success narrative is defined as the entry point into a standard life-course narrative linking good grades and university admission to stable employment, economic independence, housing, family formation, and old age. It gained institutional distribution during industrialization and educational expansion by organizing experiences of social mobility and stability. Yet higher-education massification, credential expansion, and changes in labor and housing markets have made its efficacy more conditional. School evaluation, family investment, university and labor-market selection, and textbook life-planning representations do not adjust at the same pace. This paper interprets this as a nonsynchronous breakdown rather than its disappearance.

The paper reconstructs mechanisms between macro-level structure and individual suffering often compressed into “internalization.” School structure appears as a distributive grammar in which time, attention, information, opportunities, recognition, and sanctions are attached to particular performances. Through repeated experiences of action and outcome, students develop a practice grammar organizing attention, time, and the body. When external evaluative standards are recursively applied to the self, self-interpellation emerges; when a pathway is experienced as the only route preserving safety, relationships, recognition, dignity, and the future, acute affective linkage forms. Yet structural coercion need not become a criterion of self-worth. Structural entrapment occurs when actors continue to perform because institutional distribution is high and resources for exit are limited even without believing the narrative.

These dimensions are assembled into V-Q-C coordinates to derive five mechanisms of suffering: suffering within the narrative, the double bind, anomie, structural coercion, and guilt induced by attacks on legitimacy. Distributive grammar itself is not treated as an error or violence to be eliminated, but as the institutional and phenomenological horizon through which schools allocate limited time and opportunities and students encounter worldly possibilities and risks. The problem arises when one distributive grammar monopolistically links performance evaluation to love, belonging, dignity, and the whole of life while foreclosing revision, retrying, and alternative pathways. Accordingly, Bildung is redefined as a phenomenological process of self-formation in which one is protected enough to revise one’s horizon of expectation in response to experience. Schools and teachers should limit the scope of evaluation, distinguish institutional advantage from human worth, and preserve the reversibility of failure and relational respect.

articles.title: Who Works from Home, and Who Enjoys It? Gender, Parenthood, and Affective Well-Being in Britain Before, During, and After the Covid-19 Pandemic
articles.authors: zhuofei lu; Matthew Henglong Luo; Yucheng He; Man-Yee Kan
articles.abstract:
Policy discourse in the United Kingdom presents flexible working as a remedy for
work–family conflict, with mothers and carers as its principal beneficiaries. We
ask who actually works from home, and who enjoys it, using UK Time Use Sur-
vey diaries collected before (2014–2015), during (2020–2021), and after (2023)
the Covid-19 pandemic. Uptake is measured as daily minutes of home-based paid
work and as the share of paid work performed at home; affective experience
is measured as episode-level enjoyment, modelled with two-way (person–diary)
fixed effects among non-manual employees on weekday diaries. Working from
home rose sharply during the pandemic and remained elevated in 2023, but
mothers are not its principal users: in 2023 they record the lowest uptake of the
four gender × parenthood groups. The affective evidence is period-dependent.
Before the pandemic, women report lower enjoyment when working at home
than on-site, whereas men report higher. In 2021, under lockdown, this pat-
tern inverts: mothers show the largest positive home-working association of any
group. By 2023 the lockdown pattern is gone: mothers, fathers, and childless
women all report significantly lower enjoyment when working at home, and only childless men report higher. The one period in which mothers benefited was
thus the period in which home-working was a universal mandate rather than a
statutory entitlement. Flexible-working rights alone appear insufficient to deliver
the affective benefits promised to mothers and carers; complementary care and
workplace-norm interventions are required.

articles.title: Educational and Socioeconomic Determinants of Parents’ Knowledge of Child Abuse in Egor Local Government Area of Edo State, Nigeria
articles.authors: Adriel Ekozin; Egwonor Opoggen; Obehi Destiny Elebhosele
articles.abstract: Despite the enactment of the Child Rights Act and the growing advocacy for child protection in Nigeria, child abuse is a huge public health and social welfare problem. Parents have a key role to play in protecting children but their understanding of what is child abuse may be influenced by their education and social and economic status. The study looked both educational and socioeconomic factors influencing parents' knowledge of child abuse in Egor Local Government Area of Edo State, Nigeria. Specifically, the level of parents' knowledge about child abuse and the effect of educational level and socioeconomic status on parents' knowledge were evaluated. The results showed that parents' awareness of child abuse was moderate but there were significant gaps in their knowledge of child abuse law, such as the Child Rights Act, and of non-physical forms of child abuse. It was reported that parents' knowledge of child abuse was significantly and positively related to their educational level and socioeconomic status was significantly related to their understanding and awareness of child protection issues. The study recommended that there is a need for enhanced parental education and alleviation of socioeconomic inequalities to boost child protection systems in Nigeria. It calls for increased public education initiatives, community outreach parenting education initiatives and policy-level support for prioritising the inclusion of child protection education within adult literacy, health promotion and social welfare initiatives.

articles.title: A qualitative analysis of the construction of responsible dog ownership in UK stakeholder policy and educational literature.
articles.authors: Carri Westgarth
articles.abstract: A variety of campaign and policy messages in the field of dog ownership and canine welfare centre upon the fundamental concept of ‘responsible’ ownership. However, what this is perceived to entail is unstudied, and important if the design of interventions to promote it are to be effective. Therefore, this study aimed to explore the meaning and stipulations of ‘Responsible Dog Ownership’ (RDO) within UK stakeholder literature focused on education of dog owners and the animal professionals who manage them. Primary literature concerning RDO and canine codes of practice in the UK was collected (10 documents), along with a google search for UK hits for ‘responsible dog ownership’ (16 documents). An inductive thematic analysis was performed on the 26 documents. Owners were described as having a duty, requiring commitment, to provide personalised care for the dog, by seeking out the advice of qualified professionals. Actions were required to keep the dog under control, healthy (physically and behaviourally), in a suitable environment, with appropriate identification, and not allowing the dog to foul. Perceived responsibility of the owner extended to carefully considering where and how they source a dog. Clarity of current guidance on RDO is challenging due to the advice to do different things depending on the dog and context. Owners and the professionals they seek advice from are also failing to meet the clear stipulation to use reward-based training techniques and not use aversive, punishment-based methods. This study for the first time distils multiple varied guidance into one clear set of recommendations, including a suggested ‘Are you a responsible dog owner?’ checklist. This can be used as a framework by policymakers and educators to construct more detailed localised guidance around the duties and expected behaviours of dog owners in regard to UK law and wider societal perceptions.

articles.title: From National Accounting to Macroeconomic Flows
articles.authors: Woongki Lee
articles.abstract: This study develops a macroeconomic framework that integrates the household, business, government, and foreign sectors. At the center of the analysis is the circulation of value and funds across the economy through cash flows associated with issuer-holder financing. The framework clarifies the relations among major macroeconomic aggregates. In particular, by treating money creation as part of value supply, it provides a systematic basis for analyzing how monetary operations affect transactions across sectors.

articles.title: Firm Optimization across Capital Forms
articles.authors: Woongki Lee
articles.abstract: This study derives a model of firm optimization across capital forms and incorporates the resulting optimality conditions into asset pricing. The structure of the problem depends on how profitability is modeled. When profitability is endogenous, optimization is grounded in production decisions; when profitability is exogenous, it is organized around operating profit. These alternative assumptions yield two asset pricing frameworks, each with a factor representation derived from the firm’s decision margins. By relating these representations to established pricing factors, the study provides a structured economic basis for reinterpreting established factors through firm optimization.

articles.title: A General Framework for Equity Valuation
articles.authors: Woongki Lee
articles.abstract: This study develops a general framework for equity valuation that unifies a wide range of valuation models within a coherent structure. It is built on a reformulation of key equity-related variables that preserves their economic functions, together with three exact identities that capture the fundamental links among them. These identities make it possible to derive valuation models under both fixed and revising expectations. The resulting models include not only familiar formulations but also new ones, underscoring the value of this approach for analyzing equity valuation.

articles.title: Administrative Production of Disaster Vulnerability: Explaining Persistent Infrastructure Vulnerability through Administrative Learning in the Himalayan Region
articles.authors: Vishal Thakur
articles.abstract: Public administrations in disaster-prone low- and middle-income countries face a persistent governance question: do institutions learn from one disaster to the next, or does experience fail to translate into revised policy and practice? This study addresses that question through the Administrative Production of Disaster Vulnerability (APDV), a policy-cycle framework tracing how vulnerability is reproduced or corrected across planning, budgeting, maintenance, and reconstruction, applied to Himachal Pradesh, India. PWD infrastructure damage across two successive monsoons (2023, 2025) correlates strongly across eleven districts (Pearson r = 0.819, p = 0.002; Spearman ρ = 0.882, p < 0.001), with Mandi and Shimla the highest-damage districts both years and state-wide damage rising 55.5% despite reconstruction spending. APDV distinguishes chronic vulnerability (Mandi, Shimla), a failure to convert risk into revised practice, from acute vulnerability (Chamba, Una), limited anticipatory capacity. Findings support district-specific resilience planning and identify administrative learning capacity as a distinct governance challenge.

articles.title: Pseudo-Populism as Strategic Political Communication: A Comparative Analysis of Electoral Communication and Voting Behavior in the Philippines, Brazil, India and Türkiye
articles.authors: Shaina Tingga
articles.abstract:
The growing prevalence of pseudo-populism has reshaped political campaigns across
developing countries, where candidates increasingly employ people-centered rhetoric,
anti-elite narratives, and emotionally driven messaging to secure electoral support without
consistently advancing policies aligned with the public interest. This study examines the
influence of pseudo-populist political messaging on the voting behavior of electorates in
developing democracies through a secondary quantitative data analysis. Drawing upon
existing datasets and findings from reputable electoral surveys and political behavior studies,
the research investigates the relationship between exposure to pseudo-populist appeals and
voting preferences while considering the roles of political trust, media consumption,
education, and socioeconomic conditions. Rather than assuming that voters are inherently
susceptible to populist narratives, the study explores how structural and institutional factors
shape citizens' electoral decisions. By synthesizing quantitative evidence from multiple
developing countries, the research aims to identify common patterns in voter behavior and
assess the broader implications of pseudo-populism for democratic accountability and
electoral integrity. The findings are expected to contribute to the expanding literature on
populism by providing a comparative perspective on how strategic political communication
influences electoral outcomes and by offering insights that may support civic education
initiatives, evidence-based policymaking, and the promotion of informed democratic
participation.

articles.title: The Importance of a Clear and Unambiguous Estimand for Hilbert Problems (or Any Other Empirical Research)
articles.authors: Daniel Major-Smith
articles.abstract: "Hilbert problems" are a great idea to galvanise research in the scientific study of religion, yet how do we go about answering these – or any other scientific questions of interest – empirically? This "meta-scientific" methodological aspect of research was largely missing from the original Hilbert problems and the 10 year follow-ups. Here, I want to focus on the importance of a clear and unambiguous estimand – the target quantity a study wants to estimate – and how this shapes all aspects of research, from synthesising existing research, data collection, statistical analysis and interpretation of results. At present, this is often vague or left unspecified, yet making progress on these Hilbert problems requires that researchers can clearly and unambiguously answer the question: "What is your estimand?"

articles.title: A General Framework for Tax Shield Valuation
articles.authors: Woongki Lee
articles.abstract: This study develops a general valuation framework that delivers internally consistent valuations for all forms of firm capital and for the tax shield associated with their combination. This consistency is achieved by incorporating the interdependence among the components of a levered firm’s cash flows. The study reexamines classical tax shield valuation models within the same framework and clarifies the conditions under which each arises as a special case. A central finding is that these models depend not only on stated assumptions but on an implicit assumption that debt is risk-free. This hidden assumption is more restrictive than it may appear.

articles.title: Cellular automata coupled with Bayesian MCMC reveal the evolutionary history of diffusion processes
articles.authors: Takuya Takahashi; Nico Neureiter; Geneviève Hannes; Peter Ranacher
articles.abstract: Spatial diffusion is a fundamental topic in geographic information science, relevant to various phenomena such as urban sprawl, pathogen dispersal, and the spread of innovation. When studying these processes, we often work with incomplete data. We may know the geographic distribution of the phenomenon at some specific points in time, while the full history of its diffusion is unknown. Alternatively, we may have data for certain regions but not the entire area where the diffusion occurs. We present sBread, a novel Bayesian model which infers the history of a diffusion process from temporally or spatially incomplete data. Like a stochastic cellular automaton, sBread uses probabilistic local updating rules to model how the geographic distribution of a phenomenon changes over time through local interactions. However, unlike cellular automata, which focus on forward simulation starting from a known initial state, sBread employs Markov Chain Monte Carlo (MCMC) to sample multiple plausible diffusion histories from the posterior distribution, given the observed data. Thus, sBread reconstructs the most likely past histories consistent with any observed data. We apply sBread to both simulated data and a case study on the diffusion of Indo-European languages in South America, which displaced the indigenous languages following European colonisation.

articles.title: Price Setting, Free Riding, and Equilibrium
articles.authors: Woongki Lee
articles.abstract: We analyze strategic interaction among investors by distinguishing between price taking and price setting. The analysis shows that as price setting becomes more prevalent, equilibrium prices fall. Because this lower price benefits price takers as well as price setters, price taking can be understood as free riding on price setting. The gains from the lower price are distributed more heavily toward price takers. This asymmetry creates relative-comparison concerns, which can distort incentives and discourage price setting even when it would increase aggregate utility. We examine this problem through a pricing game and derive implications for strategic behavior and equilibrium outcomes.

articles.title: A Macroeconomic Theory of Value Conversion
articles.authors: Woongki Lee
articles.abstract: This study develops a theory of value conversion in which conversion depends on realized consumption growth. By governing value conversion over time, consumption growth becomes a key determinant of output’s market value and a driver of broader economic expansion. The theory differs from conventional macroeconomic frameworks in two respects. First, it redefines production as an internal technological process combined with an external valuation process, so market-valued output depends not only on production but also on converting latent value into market value. Second, it reinterprets macroeconomic relations by treating household consumption as the starting point of causality.

articles.title: Comparative Analysis of Employee Compensation in Allegheny County, Pennsylvania, Before and After the COVID-19 Pandemic (2019-2020)
articles.authors: Sohel Sarwar; Robert King; Guelord Gabibulu
articles.abstract: The COVID-19 pandemic, which commenced in early 2020, significantly affected worldwide economies, labor markets, and employment conditions. Allegheny County, home to Pittsburgh and its surrounding areas, provides a critical case study examining how the pandemic affected local government employee compensation. Paired t-tests of salary data between 2019 and 2020 (pre- and post-COVID-19 pandemic) demonstrate a significant increase in average gross salaries for all employees of Allegheny County. While overall employee gross pays increased, the distribution of salaries became less concentrated, with a greater emphasis on higher-earning individuals. Within specific job categories, Nursing Assistants had a significantly greater salary in 2020; however, Deputy Sheriffs showed no significant change. Nursing Assistants likely worked more overtime to support the healthcare response to the pandemic. Law enforcement officers typically receive paid overtime to provide security for public events such as professional football, baseball, hockey games, and public concerts. With restrictions on these events, law enforcement officers likely faced reductions in their overtime pay in 2020. Forecasting employee salaries from 2023 to 2027 revealed a wide range in the intervals, reflecting increasing uncertainty further in the future. Due to potential variability, the forecasting results were, therefore, inconclusive.

articles.title: BLACK LGBTI+ PENTECOSTAL FAMILIES AND AFFECT OF RESISTANCE: DECOLONIAL PERSPECTIVES FROM THE BRAZILIAN PERIPHERY
articles.authors: Átila Augusto dos Santos
articles.abstract: This paper presents key results from doctoral research in Religious Studies on Black LGBTI+ Pentecostal families in Brazil, conceptualized herein as quilombo families (famílias aquilombadas), viewed as ethical-affective expressions of resistance within the religious field. Utilizing an intersectional, decolonial, and affective framework, engaging critical scholars such as Joe Coyle, E. Patrick Johnson, and Beatriz Nascimento, the study deploys the metaphor of the Pentecostal quilombo to analyze inclusive churches as urban territories of affection, freedom, and the restoration of social bonds. Grounded in semi-structured qualitative interviews with 33 Black LGBTI+ individuals and families across inclusive congregations, the findings reveal how these family units challenge traditional Christian heterocisnormative dogmas and articulate a counter-hegemonic spirituality. This framework demonstrates both the transformative potential of affective-political reconstruction and the structural limits of inclusion when racial, moral, and gender hierarchies remain unbroken.
